sentences.zh: 李憕

translations.literal: Li Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng

sentences.zh: 李憕，太原文水人。

translations.literal: Li Cheng was a native of Wenshui in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng was a native of Wenshui in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父希倩，中宗神龍初，右臺監察御史。

translations.literal: His father Xi Qian, in the early Shenlong era of Emperor Zhongzong, served as surveillance censor of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi Qian served as surveillance censor of the Right Secretariat in the early Shenlong reign of Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 憕早聰敏，以明經舉，開元初為咸陽尉。

translations.literal: Cheng was intelligent from youth; recommended on the Mingjing examination, in the early Kaiyuan era he served as magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was bright from youth. Recommended on the Mingjing examination, he became magistrate of Xianyang in the early Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 時張說自紫微令、燕國公出為相州刺史、河北按察使，有洺州劉行善相人，說問：「寮采後誰貴達？」

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yue, having left his posts as Director of the Bureau of Astrological Services and Duke of Yan, took office as prefect of Xiangzhou and Hebei investigation commissioner. There was a physiognomist of Mingzhou named Liu Xing, whom Zhang asked, "Among my staff, who will rise to eminence afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yue had left his posts as Director of the Bureau of Astrological Services and Duke of Yan to become prefect of Xiangzhou and Hebei investigation commissioner. A physiognomist of Mingzhou named Liu Xing was present, and Zhang asked him, "Among my staff, who will rise to eminence in the future?"

sentences.zh: 行乃稱憕及臨河尉鄭巖。

translations.literal: Xing then named Cheng and Zheng Yan, magistrate of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: Xing named Cheng and Zheng Yan, magistrate of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 說乃以女妻巖，妹婿陰行真女妻於憕。

translations.literal: Zhang then gave his daughter in marriage to Yan, and the daughter of his brother-in-law Yin Xingzhen in marriage to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang gave his daughter in marriage to Yan, and married the daughter of his brother-in-law Yin Xingzhen to Cheng.

sentences.zh: 及說為并州長史、天兵軍大使，引憕常在幕下。

translations.literal: When Zhang became chief administrator of Bingzhou and grand ambassador of the Tianbing Army, he brought Cheng into his staff and kept him constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang became chief administrator of Bingzhou and grand ambassador of the Tianbing Army, he kept Cheng constantly at his side on his staff.

sentences.zh: 九年，入為相，憕又為長安尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered the capital as chancellor, and Cheng again served as magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Zhang entered the capital as chancellor, and Cheng again served as magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 屬宇文融為御史，括田戶，奏知名之士崔希逸、咸廙業、宇文順、於孺卿、李宙及悽為判官，攝監察御史，分路檢察，以課並遷監察御史。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Rong became censor and conducted the household land survey, he nominated renowned men—Cui Xiyi, Xian Yiye, Yuwen Shun, Yu Ruqing, Li Zhou, and Cheng—as case judges with acting surveillance censor status, dispatched on separate routes to inspect; on the strength of their performance they were all promoted to surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Rong became censor and conducted the household land survey, he nominated renowned scholars including Cui Xiyi, Xian Yiye, Yuwen Shun, Yu Ruqing, Li Zhou, and Cheng as case judges with acting surveillance censor status, dispatched on separate inspection routes; on the strength of their performance they were all promoted to surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 憕驟歷兵、吏部郎中，給事中。

translations.literal: Cheng rose rapidly through the posts of director in the Ministries of War and Personnel, then supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng rose rapidly through director posts in the Ministries of War and Personnel to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 憕有吏幹，明於幾案，甚有當官之稱。

translations.literal: Cheng had administrative ability, was skilled at desk work, and won great praise as an official.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had administrative talent, excelled at paperwork, and won high praise as an official.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，為河南少尹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he became vice administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he became vice administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時蕭炅為尹，依倚權貴，蒞事多不法。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Jiong was administrator; relying on powerful patrons, he conducted affairs in many unlawful ways.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Jiong was administrator; relying on powerful patrons, he conducted affairs in many unlawful ways.

sentences.zh: 憕以公直正之，人用繫賴。

translations.literal: Cheng corrected him with public integrity, and people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng corrected him with public integrity, and the people came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 又道士孫甑生以左道求進，托以修功德，往來嵩山，求請無度，憕必挫之。

translations.literal: Moreover the Daoist Sun Zhensheng sought advancement through heterodox practices, claiming to perform meritorious rites; traveling to and from Mount Song, he made boundless requests, and Cheng always thwarted him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Daoist Sun Zhensheng sought advancement through heterodox practices, claiming to perform meritorious rites; traveling to and from Mount Song he made boundless requests, and Cheng always thwarted him.

sentences.zh: 炅及甑生患之，而構於朝廷。

translations.literal: Jiong and Zhensheng resented this and slandered him at court.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong and Zhensheng resented this and slandered him at court.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，出為清河太守。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era he was sent out as prefect of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao era he was sent out as prefect of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 十一載，累轉河東太守、本道采訪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred in succession to prefect of Hedong and investigation commissioner of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred in succession to prefect of Hedong and investigation commissioner of that circuit.

sentences.zh: 謁於行在所，改尚書右丞、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He presented himself at the temporary imperial residence and was reassigned as vice director of the Ministry of Rites and metropolitan magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself at the temporary imperial residence and was reassigned as vice director of the Ministry of Rites and metropolitan magistrate.

sentences.zh: 十四載，轉光祿卿、東京留守，判尚書省事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and resident guardian of the Eastern Capital, with concurrent authority over the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and resident guardian of the Eastern Capital, with concurrent authority over the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其載十一月，安祿山反於范陽，人心震懼。

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang, and hearts throughout the realm trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the eleventh month An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang, and hearts throughout the realm trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 玄宗遣安西節度封常清兼御史大夫為將，召募於東京以禦之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong dispatched Feng Changqing, military commissioner of Anxi and concurrently censor-in-chief, as general, to recruit troops at the Eastern Capital to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong dispatched Feng Changqing, military commissioner of Anxi and concurrently censor-in-chief, as general to recruit troops at the Eastern Capital to resist him.

sentences.zh: 憕與留臺御史中丞盧奕、河南尹達奚珣，綏輯將士，完繕城郭，遏其侵逼。

translations.literal: Cheng, together with Lu Yi, surveillance censor-in-chief of the resident court, and Daqi Xida, metropolitan magistrate of Henan, pacified the troops, repaired the walls and moats, and checked the enemy's advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, together with Lu Yi, surveillance censor-in-chief of the resident court, and Daqi Xida, metropolitan magistrate of Henan, pacified the troops, repaired the walls and moats, and checked the enemy advance.

sentences.zh: 遷憕禮部尚書，依前留守。

translations.literal: Cheng was promoted to minister of rites while continuing as resident guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was promoted to minister of rites while continuing as resident guardian.

sentences.zh: 自逆徒發范陽，至渡河，令嚴，覘候計絕。

translations.literal: From the time the rebels set out from Fanyang until they crossed the river, their orders were strict and scouting plans were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the rebels set out from Fanyang until they crossed the river, their orders were strict and scouting plans were cut off.

sentences.zh: 及渡河，陷陳留、滎陽二郡，殺張介然、崔無诐，數日間已至都城下。

translations.literal: Once they crossed the river they captured the two prefectures of Chenliu and Xingyang, killed Zhang Jieran and Cui Wubi, and within a few days had reached the walls of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Once they crossed the river they captured the prefectures of Chenliu and Xingyang, killed Zhang Jieran and Cui Wubi, and within a few days reached the walls of the capital.

sentences.zh: 祿山所統，皆蕃漢精兵，訓練已久；

translations.literal: Those under Lushan's command were all elite troops, both foreign and Han, long trained in warfare;
translations.idiomatic: Those under Lushan's command were all elite troops, both foreign and Han, long trained in warfare;

sentences.zh: 常清之眾，多市井之人，初不知戰。

translations.literal: Changqing's forces were mostly townsmen who at first knew nothing of battle.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing's forces were mostly townspeople who at first knew nothing of battle.

sentences.zh: 及兵交之後，被鐵騎唐突，飛矢如雨，皆魂懾色沮，望賊奔散。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined, iron cavalry charged them headlong and flying arrows fell like rain; all were terrified in spirit and pale in face, and at sight of the enemy they fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Once battle was joined, iron cavalry charged them headlong and arrows fell like rain; all were terrified in spirit and pale in face, and at sight of the enemy they fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 憕謂奕曰：「吾曹荷國重寄，誓無避死，雖力不敵，其若官守何！」

translations.literal: Cheng said to Yi, "We bear the state's heavy trust and swear not to flee death; though our strength cannot match theirs, what of our official duty!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said to Yi, "We bear the state's heavy trust and swear not to flee death. Though our strength cannot match theirs, what of our official duty!"

sentences.zh: 奕亦便許願守本司。

translations.literal: Yi also readily agreed to hold his own office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi also readily agreed to hold his own office.

sentences.zh: 於是憕居留守宅，奕獨居臺中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cheng remained in the guardian's residence while Yi alone stayed in the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Cheng remained in the guardian's residence while Yi alone stayed in the censorate.

sentences.zh: 及常清西奔，祿山領其眾，椎鼓大呼，以入都城，殺掠數千人，箭及宮闕。

translations.literal: When Changqing fled west, Lushan led his forces, beating drums and shouting loudly, into the capital city, killing and plundering several thousand people; arrows reached the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: When Changqing fled west, Lushan led his forces, beating drums and shouting loudly, into the capital city, killing and plundering several thousand people; arrows reached the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 然後住居於閑廄中，令擒悽及奕、判官蔣清等三人，害之，以威於眾。

translations.literal: Then he halted in the idle stables and ordered Cheng, Yi, and the case officer Jiang Qing seized and killed to intimidate the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Then he halted in the idle stables and ordered Cheng, Yi, and the case officer Jiang Qing seized and killed to intimidate the multitude.

sentences.zh: 祿山傳悽、奕、清三人之首，以徇河北。

translations.literal: Lushan sent the heads of Cheng, Yi, and Qing through Hebei as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan sent the heads of Cheng, Yi, and Qing through Hebei as a warning.

sentences.zh: 信宿，至平原，太守顏真卿斬其使，浴其首，殮以木函，祭而瘞之，以聞。

translations.literal: After one night they reached Pingyuan; Prefect Yan Zhenqing executed the envoy, bathed the heads, encoffined them in wooden boxes, offered sacrifice and buried them, and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: After one night they reached Pingyuan; Prefect Yan Zhenqing executed the envoy, bathed the heads, encoffined them in wooden boxes, offered sacrifice and buried them, and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 玄宗贈悽司徒，仍與一子五品官。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong posthumously enfeoffed Cheng as grand mentor of state and granted one son the rank of fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong posthumously enfeoffed Cheng as grand mentor of state and granted one son the rank of fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 奕武部尚書，崔無诐工部尚書，各與一子官。

translations.literal: Yi was made minister of war, Cui Wubi minister of works; each was granted an office for one son.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was made minister of war and Cui Wubi minister of works; each was granted an office for one son.

sentences.zh: 蔣清文部郎中。

translations.literal: Jiang Qing was made director in the Ministry of Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qing was made director in the Ministry of Civil Affairs.

sentences.zh: 憕豐於產業，伊川膏腴，水陸上田，修竹茂樹，自城及闕口，別業相望，與吏部侍郎李彭年皆有地癖。

translations.literal: Cheng was wealthy in estates; fertile lands on the Yichuan, fields of superior grade by water and land, bamboo groves and thick woods—from the city to the pass his separate estates stood in sight of one another; he and Vice Minister of Personnel Li Pengnian both had a passion for land.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was wealthy in estates: fertile lands on the Yichuan, fields of superior grade by water and land, bamboo groves and thick woods—from the city to the pass his separate estates stood in sight of one another. He and Vice Minister of Personnel Li Pengnian both had a passion for land.

sentences.zh: 鄭巖，天寶中仕至絳郡太守，入為少府監，田產亞於憕。

translations.literal: Zheng Yan, in the Tianbao era, rose to prefect of Jiang Commandery, entered the capital as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and his estates were second only to Cheng's.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yan, in the Tianbao era, rose to prefect of Jiang Commandery, entered the capital as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and his estates were second only to Cheng's.

sentences.zh: 憕有子十餘人，二子為僧，與憕同遇害；

translations.literal: Cheng had more than ten sons; two became monks and were killed together with Cheng;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had more than ten sons; two became monks and were killed together with Cheng;

sentences.zh: 二子彭、源，存焉。

translations.literal: two sons, Peng and Yuan, survived.
translations.idiomatic: two sons, Peng and Yuan, survived.

sentences.zh: 子 源

translations.literal: Son: Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yuan

sentences.zh: 源，時年八歲，為賊所俘，轉徙流離，凡七八年。

translations.literal: Yuan, then eight years old, was captured by the rebels and wandered in displacement for seven or eight years altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, then eight years old, was captured by the rebels and wandered in displacement for seven or eight years altogether.

sentences.zh: 及史朝義走河北，洛陽故吏有義源者，贖之於民家。

translations.literal: When Shi Chaoyi fled to Hebei, an old Luoyang official named Yiyuan redeemed him from a commoner's household.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Chaoyi fled to Hebei, an old Luoyang official named Yiyuan redeemed him from a commoner's household.

sentences.zh: 代宗聞之，授河南府參軍，轉司農寺主簿。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong heard of this and appointed him adjutant of Henan Prefecture, then transferred him to chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong heard of this and appointed him adjutant of Henan Prefecture, then transferred him to chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Granary.

sentences.zh: 以父死禍難，無心祿仕，誓不婚妻，不食酒肉。

translations.literal: Because his father had died in national calamity, he had no heart for office or salary; he vowed never to marry, and ate neither wine nor meat.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died in national calamity, he had no heart for office or salary; he vowed never to marry and ate neither wine nor meat.

sentences.zh: 洛陽之北惠林寺，憕之舊堅墅也，源乃依寺僧，寓居一室，依僧齋戒，人未嘗見其所習。

translations.literal: Huilin Temple north of Luoyang was Cheng's old fortified villa; Yuan then relied on the temple monks, lodging in one room and following monastic abstinences—people never saw what he practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Huilin Temple north of Luoyang was Cheng's old fortified villa; Yuan relied on the temple monks, lodging in one room and following monastic abstinences—people never saw what he practiced.

sentences.zh: 先穴地為墓，預為終制，時時偃仰於穴中。

translations.literal: He first dug the ground for a tomb, prepared his funeral arrangements in advance, and from time to time lay down in the pit.
translations.idiomatic: He first dug the ground for a tomb, prepared his funeral arrangements in advance, and from time to time lay down in the pit.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年，御史中丞李德裕表薦之曰：「處士李源，即故禮部尚書、東都留守、贈司徒、忠烈公李憕之少子。

translations.literal: In the third year of Changqing, Censor-in-Chief Li Deyu memorialized recommending him, saying, "The recluse Li Yuan is the youngest son of the late Minister of Rites, Eastern Capital resident guardian, posthumously enfeoffed Grand Mentor of State and Duke of Loyal Valor Li Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changqing, Censor-in-Chief Li Deyu memorialized recommending him, saying, "The recluse Li Yuan is the youngest son of the late Minister of Rites, Eastern Capital resident guardian, posthumously enfeoffed Grand Mentor of State and Duke of Loyal Valor Li Cheng.

sentences.zh: 天與忠孝，嗣茲貞烈。

translations.literal: Heaven endowed him with loyalty and filial piety, inheriting this steadfast valor.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven endowed him with loyalty and filial piety, inheriting this steadfast valor.

sentences.zh: 以父死國難，哀纏終身，自司農寺主簿，絕心祿仕，垂五十年。

translations.literal: Because his father died in the nation's crisis, grief bound him for life; from chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Granary he renounced office and salary, for nearly fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father died in the nation's crisis, grief bound him for life; from chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Granary he renounced office and salary for nearly fifty years.

sentences.zh: 暨於衰暮，多依惠林佛寺，本憕之墅也。

translations.literal: In his declining years he dwelt mostly at Huilin Buddhist Temple—Cheng's old villa.
translations.idiomatic: In his declining years he dwelt mostly at Huilin Buddhist Temple—Cheng's old villa.

sentences.zh: 寺之正殿，即悽之寢室，源過殿必趨，未嘗登踐。

translations.literal: The temple's main hall was Cheng's sleeping chamber; Yuan always hurried past the hall and never once stepped upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The temple's main hall was Cheng's sleeping chamber; Yuan always hurried past the hall and never once stepped upon it.

sentences.zh: 隨僧一食，已五十年。

translations.literal: He ate one meal with the monks, as he had for fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: He ate one meal with the monks, as he had for fifty years.

sentences.zh: 其端心執孝，無有不至。

translations.literal: His upright heart and practiced filial piety were without limit.
translations.idiomatic: His upright heart and practiced filial piety were without limit.

sentences.zh: 抱此貞節，棄於清朝，臣竊為陛下惜之。」

translations.literal: Holding this steadfast integrity, he was cast aside by the enlightened court—I, your servant, grieve for Your Majesty's sake."
translations.idiomatic: Holding this steadfast integrity, he was cast aside by the enlightened court—I, your servant, grieve for Your Majesty's sake."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict said:

sentences.zh: 《禮》著死綏，《傳》稱握節，捐生守位，取重人倫。

translations.literal: The Rites prescribe dying in harness; the Chronicles praise grasping the tally—sacrificing life to hold one's post, weighty in human relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites prescribe dying in harness; the Chronicles praise grasping the tally—sacrificing life to hold one's post, weighty in human relations.

sentences.zh: 為義甚明，其風或替，言念於此，慨然興懷。

translations.literal: The meaning of righteousness is very clear, yet its wind may fade; thinking of this, one is moved to deep feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of righteousness is very clear, yet its wind may fade; thinking of this, one is moved to deep feeling.

sentences.zh: 而朝之公卿，有上言者，云天寶之季，盜起幽陵，振蕩生靈，噬吞河洛。

translations.literal: Yet among the court's ministers some have submitted that in the late Tianbao era bandits rose in Youling, shaking the living and devouring the Yellow and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among the court's ministers some have submitted that in the late Tianbao era bandits rose in Youling, shaking the living and devouring the Yellow and Luo.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒、忠烈公憕，處難居首，正色受屠，兩河聞風，再固危壁，首立殊節，到今稱之。

translations.literal: The posthumously enfeoffed Grand Mentor of State and Duke of Loyal Valor Cheng, facing hardship at the fore, received execution with stern countenance; hearing of it through the two He, the perilous walls were twice strengthened; he first established extraordinary integrity, praised to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumously enfeoffed Grand Mentor of State and Duke of Loyal Valor Cheng, facing hardship at the fore, received execution with stern countenance; hearing of it through the two He, the perilous walls were twice strengthened; he first established extraordinary integrity, praised to this day.

sentences.zh: 其子源，有曾、閔之行，可貫於神明；

translations.literal: His son Yuan has the conduct of Zeng and Min, fit to pierce the spirits;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan has the conduct of Zeng and Min, fit to pierce the spirits;

sentences.zh: 有巢、由之風，可希於太古。

translations.literal: the wind of Chao and You, rare since high antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: the wind of Chao and You, rare since high antiquity.

sentences.zh: 山林以寄其跡，爵祿不入於心，泊然無營，五十餘載。

translations.literal: He entrusted his footsteps to mountains and forests; rank and salary did not enter his heart—tranquil and without pursuit, for more than fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted his footsteps to mountains and forests; rank and salary did not enter his heart—tranquil and without pursuit, for more than fifty years.

sentences.zh: 夫褒忠可以勸臣節，旌孝可以激人倫，尚義可以警澆浮，敬老可以厚風俗。

translations.literal: To honor loyalty can encourage ministerial integrity; to signal filial piety can stir human relations; to esteem righteousness can warn against decadence; to respect the aged can enrich custom.
translations.idiomatic: To honor loyalty can encourage ministerial integrity; to signal filial piety can stir human relations; to esteem righteousness can warn against decadence; to respect the aged can enrich custom.

sentences.zh: 舉茲四者，大儆於時。

translations.literal: Raising these four is a great warning for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Raising these four is a great warning for the age.

sentences.zh: 是用擢自衡門，立於文陛，處以諫職，冀聞讜言，仍加印紱，式示光寵。

translations.literal: Therefore we promote him from the humble gate to stand in the literary hall, place him in remonstrance office in hope of hearing forthright words, and further grant seals and ribbons to display favor.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we promote him from the humble gate to stand in the literary hall, place him in remonstrance office in hope of hearing forthright words, and further grant seals and ribbons to display favor.

sentences.zh: 可守左諫議大夫，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: He may serve as Left Remonstrance Official and be granted the crimson fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: He may serve as Left Remonstrance Official and be granted the crimson fish tally.

sentences.zh: 仍敕河南尹差官就所居敦諭遣發。

translations.literal: The Henan metropolitan magistrate is further ordered to dispatch an official to his residence to instruct and urge his departure.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan metropolitan magistrate is further ordered to dispatch an official to his residence to instruct and urge his departure.

sentences.zh: 穆宗尋令中使賫手詔、緋袍、牙笏、絹二百匹，往洛陽惠林寺宣賜。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong soon ordered a palace envoy to bear an imperial handwritten edict, crimson robe, ivory tally, and two hundred bolts of silk to Huilin Temple in Luoyang to bestow them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong soon ordered a palace envoy to bear an imperial handwritten edict, crimson robe, ivory tally, and two hundred bolts of silk to Huilin Temple in Luoyang to bestow them.

sentences.zh: 源受詔，對中使苦陳疾甚年高，不能趨拜，附表謝恩，其官告服色絹，皆辭不受。

translations.literal: Yuan received the edict and, facing the palace envoy, earnestly pleaded grave illness and advanced age, unable to hurry and bow; he appended a memorial thanking the grace, and declined the commission, robes, colors, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan received the edict and, facing the palace envoy, earnestly pleaded grave illness and advanced age, unable to hurry and bow; he appended a memorial thanking the grace and declined the commission, robes, colors, and silk.

sentences.zh: 竟卒於寺。

translations.literal: He finally died in the temple.
translations.idiomatic: He finally died in the temple.

sentences.zh: 子 彭

translations.literal: Son: Peng
translations.idiomatic: Son: Peng

sentences.zh: 彭，以一子官累歷州縣令長。

translations.literal: Peng, through offices granted one son, served in succession as prefect and magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Peng, through offices granted one son, served in succession as prefect and magistrate.

sentences.zh: 子宏，仕官愈卑。

translations.literal: His son Hong held offices ever more humble.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong held offices ever more humble.

sentences.zh: 生三子：景讓、景莊、景溫，自元和後，相繼以進士登第。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Jingrang, Jingzhuang, and Jingwen; from the Yuanhe era onward they passed the jinshi examination in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Jingrang, Jingzhuang, and Jingwen; from the Yuanhe era onward they passed the jinshi examination in succession.

sentences.zh: 彭孫 景讓

translations.literal: Peng's grandson: Jingrang
translations.idiomatic: Peng's grandson: Jingrang

sentences.zh: 景讓，太和中為尚書郎，出為商州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingrang, in the Taihe era served as director in the Secretariat, then went out as prefect of Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang, in the Taihe era served as director in the Secretariat, then went out as prefect of Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，入朝為中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he entered court as drafting official of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaicheng he entered court as drafting official of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，出為華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year he went out as prefect of Huazhou, defender of Tong Pass, and military commissioner of Zhenguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year he went out as prefect of Huazhou, defender of Tong Pass, and military commissioner of Zhenguo Army.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered court as vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he entered court as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，選貢士李蔚，後至宰相；

translations.literal: In the fifth year he selected presented scholar Li Wei, who later became chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he selected presented scholar Li Wei, who later became chancellor;

sentences.zh: 楊知退為尚書。

translations.literal: Yang Zhitui became director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhitui became director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大中朝，為襄州刺史、山南道節度使，入為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong era he served as prefect of Xiangzhou and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, then entered court as minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era he served as prefect of Xiangzhou and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, then entered court as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一年，轉御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 景讓有大志，事親以孝聞，正色立朝，言無避忌。

translations.literal: Jingrang had great ambition, was known for filial service to parents, stood in court with stern countenance, and spoke without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang had great ambition, was known for filial service to parents, stood in court with stern countenance, and spoke without evasion.

sentences.zh: 為大夫時，宣宗舅鄭光卒，詔贈司徒，罷朝三日。

translations.literal: When he was censor-in-chief, Emperor Xuanzong's maternal uncle Zheng Guang died; an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as grand mentor of state and suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When he was censor-in-chief, Emperor Xuanzong's maternal uncle Zheng Guang died; an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as grand mentor of state and suspended court for three days.

sentences.zh: 景讓曰：「國舅雖親，朝典有素，無容過越。」

translations.literal: Jingrang said, "Though the empress dowager's kin is close, court precedent has its constant measure—there must be no exceeding it."
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang said, "Though the empress dowager's kin is close, court precedent has its constant measure—there must be no exceeding it."

sentences.zh: 乃上言曰：

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 鄭光是陛下親舅，外族之愛，誠軫聖心，況皇太后哀切之時，理合加等，而賜之粟帛，隆其第宅，自家刑國，允謂合宜。

translations.literal: Zheng Guang is Your Majesty's maternal uncle; love for maternal kin truly moves the imperial heart. Moreover at a time when the empress dowager grieves deeply, it is fitting to add honors, and gifts of grain and cloth and enlargement of his residence, disciplining the family to govern the state, are altogether appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Guang is Your Majesty's maternal uncle; love for maternal kin truly moves the imperial heart. Moreover at a time when the empress dowager grieves deeply, it is fitting to add honors, and gifts of grain and cloth and enlargement of his residence, disciplining the family to govern the state, are altogether appropriate.

sentences.zh: 今以輟朝之數，比於親王公主，則前例所無。

translations.literal: Now to suspend court for a number of days comparable to imperial princes and princesses has no precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Now to suspend court for a number of days comparable to imperial princes and princesses has no precedent.

sentences.zh: 縱有，亦不可施用。

translations.literal: Even if there were one, it could not be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Even if there were one, it could not be applied.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 先王制禮，所以防微。

translations.literal: The former kings made ritual to guard against minute faults.
translations.idiomatic: The former kings made ritual to guard against minute faults.

sentences.zh: 大凡人情，於外族則深，於宗屬則薄。

translations.literal: Generally in human feeling, toward maternal kin one is deep, toward agnatic kin thin.
translations.idiomatic: Generally in human feeling, toward maternal kin one is deep, toward agnatic kin thin.

sentences.zh: 所以先王制禮，割愛厚親，士庶猶然，況當萬乘！

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings made ritual, cutting love to thicken kinship; commoners are still so—how much more the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the former kings made ritual, cutting love to thicken kinship; commoners are still so—how much more the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 親王公主，宗屬也；

translations.literal: Imperial princes and princesses are agnatic kin;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and princesses are agnatic kin;

sentences.zh: 舅氏，外族也。

translations.literal: maternal uncles are maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: maternal uncles are maternal kin.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷公卿以至庶人，據《開元禮》，外祖父母及親舅喪服，小功五月，若親伯叔親兄弟即服齊缞周年。

translations.literal: Now from court ministers down to commoners, according to the Kaiyuan Rites, mourning for maternal grandparents and maternal uncles is small merit for five months; for paternal uncles and brothers it is full mourning for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Now from court ministers down to commoners, according to the Kaiyuan Rites, mourning for maternal grandparents and maternal uncles is small merit for five months; for paternal uncles and brothers it is full mourning for one year.

sentences.zh: 所以疏其外而密於內也。

translations.literal: Thus the outer is made distant and the inner close.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the outer is made distant and the inner close.

sentences.zh: 有天下者，尤不可使外戚強盛。

translations.literal: Those who possess the realm must especially not let maternal kin grow powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Those who possess the realm must especially not let maternal kin grow powerful.

sentences.zh: 故西漢有呂氏之侈，幾滅劉氏；

translations.literal: Thus in Western Han the Lü clan's extravagance nearly extinguished the Liu house;
translations.idiomatic: Thus in Western Han the Lü clan's extravagance nearly extinguished the Liu house;

sentences.zh: 國朝有則天之篡，殆革唐命。

translations.literal: in our dynasty Empress Wu's usurpation nearly changed the Tang mandate.
translations.idiomatic: in our dynasty Empress Wu's usurpation nearly changed the Tang mandate.

sentences.zh: 皆非一朝一夕，其所由來漸也。

translations.literal: Neither came in a day or night; each arose gradually over time.
translations.idiomatic: Neither came in a day or night; each arose gradually over time.

sentences.zh: 今鄭光輟朝日數，與親王公主同，設使陛下速改詔命，輟朝一日或兩日，示其升降有差，恩禮無僭，使四方見陛下欽明之德，青史傳陛下制度之文，垂之百王，播之芳烈。

translations.literal: Now if the days of court suspension for Zheng Guang equal those for imperial princes and princesses, suppose Your Majesty swiftly alters the edict and suspends court one or two days, showing gradation in ascent and descent so favor and ritual do not transgress—then the four quarters will see Your Majesty's reverent clarity, and the blue annals will transmit Your Majesty's institutional text, handed down through a hundred kings and broadcast in fragrant deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Now if the days of court suspension for Zheng Guang equal those for imperial princes and princesses, suppose Your Majesty swiftly alters the edict and suspends court one or two days, showing gradation in ascent and descent so favor and ritual do not transgress—then the four quarters will see Your Majesty's reverent clarity, and the blue annals will transmit Your Majesty's institutional text, handed down through a hundred kings and broadcast in fragrant deeds.

sentences.zh: 臣愚不肖，謬竊恩私，實願陛下處於堯、舜之上，羲、軒之列，所以甘心鼎鑊，伏進危言！

translations.literal: I, your servant, am foolish and unworthy, wrongly enjoying private favor; I truly wish Your Majesty to stand above Yao and Shun, in the company of Xi and Xuan—therefore I gladly accept the cauldron, submitting stern words!
translations.idiomatic: I, your servant, am foolish and unworthy, wrongly enjoying private favor; I truly wish Your Majesty to stand above Yao and Shun, in the company of Xi and Xuan—therefore I gladly accept the cauldron, submitting stern words!

sentences.zh: 優詔報之，乃罷兩日。

translations.literal: A gracious edict replied to him, and court was suspended for only two days.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict replied to him, and court was suspended for only two days.

sentences.zh: 景讓復為吏部尚書，卒，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: Jingrang again became minister of personnel and died; his posthumous title was Filial.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrang again became minister of personnel and died; his posthumous title was Filial.

sentences.zh: 景溫，登第後踐歷臺閣。

translations.literal: Jingwen, after passing the examination, served in succession in the central offices.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen, after passing the examination, served in succession in the central offices.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，自工部侍郎出為華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍使。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era he went out from vice minister of works as prefect of Huazhou, defender of Tong Pass, and military commissioner of Zhenguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong era he went out from vice minister of works as prefect of Huazhou, defender of Tong Pass, and military commissioner of Zhenguo Army.

sentences.zh: 景莊，亦至達官。

translations.literal: Jingzhuang also rose to high office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhuang also rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 張介然

translations.literal: Zhang Jieran
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jieran

sentences.zh: 張介然者，蒲州猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jieran was a native of Yishi in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jieran was a native of Yishi in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 本名六朗。

translations.literal: His original name was Liulang.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Liulang.

sentences.zh: 謹慎善籌算，為郡守在河、隴。

translations.literal: Cautious and skilled at calculation, he served as prefectural administrator on the He and Long circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Cautious and skilled at calculation, he served as prefectural administrator on the He and Long circuits.

sentences.zh: 及天寶中，王忠嗣、皇甫惟明、哥舒翰相次為節將，並委以營田支度等使。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era Wang Zhongsi, Huangfu Weiming, and Geshu Han served in succession as military commissioners, all entrusting him as commissioner of garrison fields and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era Wang Zhongsi, Huangfu Weiming, and Geshu Han served in succession as military commissioners, all entrusting him as commissioner of garrison fields and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 進位衛尉卿，仍兼行軍司馬，使如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Court of the Imperial Stud while continuing as acting army marshal with duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Court of the Imperial Stud while continuing as acting army marshal with duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 及加銀青光祿大夫，帶上柱國，因入奏稱旨，特加賜賫。

translations.literal: When he was further granted silver and blue light grandee of the imperial court with supreme pillar of state rank, he entered court to report and pleased the emperor, who specially added gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When he was further granted silver and blue light grandee of the imperial court with supreme pillar of state rank, he entered court to report and pleased the emperor, who specially added gifts.

sentences.zh: 介然乘間奏曰：「臣今三品，合列棨戟。

translations.literal: Jieran seized the moment and memorialized, "I am now third rank and should display halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Jieran seized the moment and memorialized, "I am now third rank and should display halberds.

sentences.zh: 若列於帝城，鄉里不知臣貴。

translations.literal: If displayed in the imperial city, my home district would not know my honor.
translations.idiomatic: If displayed in the imperial city, my home district would not know my honor.

sentences.zh: 臣，河東人也，請列戟於故鄉。」

translations.literal: I am a man of Hedong; I ask that halberds be displayed in my native place."
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of Hedong; I ask that halberds be displayed in my native place."

sentences.zh: 玄宗曰：「所給可列故鄉，京城佇當別賜。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said, "What is granted may be displayed in the native place; for the capital a separate grant will await."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong said, "What is granted may be displayed in the native place; for the capital a separate grant will await."

sentences.zh: 介然拜謝而出，仍賜絹五百匹，令宴集閭里，以寵異之。

translations.literal: Jieran bowed in thanks and withdrew; he was further granted five hundred bolts of silk and ordered to feast his neighborhood in special honor.
translations.idiomatic: Jieran bowed in thanks and withdrew; he was further granted five hundred bolts of silk and ordered to feast his neighborhood in special honor.

sentences.zh: 本鄉列戟，自介然始也。

translations.literal: Display of halberds in one's native place began with Jieran.
translations.idiomatic: Display of halberds in one's native place began with Jieran.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰追在西京，薦為少府監。

translations.literal: Geshu Han, pursuing west to the Western Capital, recommended him as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, pursuing west to the Western Capital, recommended him as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 安祿山將犯河洛，以介然為河南防禦使，令守陳留。

translations.literal: When An Lushan was about to invade the He and Luo region, he appointed Jieran defense commissioner of Henan and ordered him to hold Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan was about to invade the He and Luo region, he appointed Jieran defense commissioner of Henan and ordered him to hold Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 陳留水陸所湊，邑居萬家，而素不習戰。

translations.literal: Chenliu was a gathering point by water and land, with ten thousand households, yet long unused to warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu was a gathering point by water and land, with ten thousand households, yet long unused to warfare.

sentences.zh: 介然至任數日，賊已渡河。

translations.literal: Within a few days of Jieran's arrival the rebels had already crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days of Jieran's arrival the rebels had already crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 雖率兵登城，兼守要害，虜騎十萬，所過殺戮，煙塵亙天，彌漫數十里。

translations.literal: Though he led troops up the walls and also guarded key points, a hundred thousand mounted raiders passed, killing wherever they went; dust and smoke filled the sky and spread for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Though he led troops up the walls and also guarded key points, a hundred thousand mounted raiders passed, killing wherever they went; dust and smoke filled the sky and spread for several tens of li.

sentences.zh: 介然之眾，聞吹角鼓噪之聲，授甲不得，氣已奪矣，故至覆敗。

translations.literal: Jieran's forces, hearing the sound of horns and war drums, could not even take up armor—their spirit was already broken—so they were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jieran's forces, hearing the sound of horns and war drums, could not even take up armor—their spirit was already broken—so they were utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 初，玄宗以祿山起逆，於河南要路懸榜以購其首，又諭已殺其子慶宗等。

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Xuanzong, because Lushan had risen in rebellion, posted rewards at key points in Henan for his head, and announced that his son Qingzong and others had already been killed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Xuanzong, because Lushan had risen in rebellion, posted rewards at key points in Henan for his head, and announced that his son Qingzong and others had already been killed.

sentences.zh: 祿山入陳留北郭，安慶緒見榜，白於祿山。

translations.literal: Lushan entered the north suburb of Chenliu; An Qingxu saw the placard and reported it to Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan entered the north suburb of Chenliu; An Qingxu saw the placard and reported it to Lushan.

sentences.zh: 祿山於輿中兩手撫胸，大哭數聲，曰：「我有何罪，已殺我兒？」

translations.literal: Lushan in his carriage clutched his chest with both hands, wept loudly several times, and said, "What crime have I committed, that my son was already killed?"
translations.idiomatic: Lushan in his carriage clutched his chest with both hands, wept loudly several times, and said, "What crime have I committed, that my son was already killed?"

sentences.zh: 便縱兇毒。

translations.literal: Then he unleashed savage cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Then he unleashed savage cruelty.

sentences.zh: 前有陳留兵將降者向萬人，行列於路，祿山命其牙將殺戮皆盡，流血如川。

translations.literal: Ahead were nearly ten thousand Chenliu soldiers about to surrender, lined along the road; Lushan ordered his guard officers to slaughter them all, and blood flowed like a river.
translations.idiomatic: Ahead were nearly ten thousand Chenliu soldiers about to surrender, lined along the road; Lushan ordered his guard officers to slaughter them all, and blood flowed like a river.

sentences.zh: 乃斬介然於軍門，祿山氣乃稍解。

translations.literal: He then beheaded Jieran at the army gate, and Lushan's rage slightly eased.
translations.idiomatic: He then beheaded Jieran at the army gate, and Lushan's rage slightly eased.

sentences.zh: 頓軍於陳留郭下，以其將李庭望為節度鎮之。

translations.literal: He halted the army below the Chenliu wall and appointed his general Li Tingwang military commissioner to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He halted the army below the Chenliu wall and appointed his general Li Tingwang military commissioner to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 十五載，玄宗贈介然工部尚書，與一子五品官。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Emperor Xuanzong posthumously enfeoffed Jieran as minister of works and granted one son the rank of fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Emperor Xuanzong posthumously enfeoffed Jieran as minister of works and granted one son the rank of fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 崔無詖

translations.literal: Cui Wubi
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wubi

sentences.zh: 崔無詖者，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Cui Wubi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wubi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 本博陵舊族。

translations.literal: Originally of the old Boling clan.
translations.idiomatic: Originally of the old Boling clan.

sentences.zh: 父從禮，中宗韋庶人之舅，景龍中衛尉卿。

translations.literal: His father Congli, maternal uncle of Empress Wei the commoner of Emperor Zhongzong, served as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud in the Jinglong era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Congli, maternal uncle of Empress Wei the commoner of Emperor Zhongzong, served as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud in the Jinglong era.

sentences.zh: 時中書令、酂國公蕭至忠才位素高，甚承恩顧，敕亡先女冥婚韋庶人亡弟。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Minister and Duke of Zan Xiao Zhizhong's talent and position were always high and he enjoyed great favor; an edict arranged a posthumous marriage between his deceased daughter and the deceased younger brother of Empress Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chief Minister and Duke of Zan Xiao Zhizhong's talent and position were always high and he enjoyed great favor; an edict arranged a posthumous marriage between his deceased daughter and the deceased younger brother of Empress Wei.

sentences.zh: 無詖婚至忠女，後為女家，中宗為兒家，供擬甚厚，時人為之語曰：「皇后嫁女，天子娶婦。」

translations.literal: Wubi married Zhizhong's daughter and later became the bride's family; Emperor Zhongzong was the groom's family, with provisions very lavish—people at the time said, "The empress marries off a daughter; the Son of Heaven takes a wife."
translations.idiomatic: Wubi married Zhizhong's daughter and later became the bride's family; Emperor Zhongzong was the groom's family, with provisions very lavish—people at the time said, "The empress marries off a daughter; the Son of Heaven takes a wife."

sentences.zh: 及韋庶人敗，至忠女亦死，無詖坐累久貶在外。

translations.literal: When Empress Wei fell, Zhizhong's daughter also died; Wubi was implicated and long demoted outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei fell, Zhizhong's daughter also died; Wubi was implicated and long demoted outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為益州司馬。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he served as vice prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era he served as vice prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 會楊國忠為新都尉，與之歡甚，國忠因事引用之，累轉陜郡太守、少府監、滎陽郡太守。

translations.literal: When Yang Guozhong was magistrate of Xindu he was on very friendly terms with him; Guozhong later cited him in office, and he was transferred in succession to prefect of Shaan Commandery, director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and prefect of Xingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong was magistrate of Xindu he was on very friendly terms with him; Guozhong later cited him in office, and he was transferred in succession to prefect of Shaan Commandery, director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and prefect of Xingyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 安祿山率眾南向，無詖召募拒之。

translations.literal: An Lushan led his forces south; Wubi recruited troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan led his forces south; Wubi recruited troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 及賊陷陳留郡後，兇威轉盛，戈矛鼓角，驚駭城邑，兩宿及滎陽。

translations.literal: After the rebels captured Chenliu Commandery their ferocious might grew still greater; spears, halberds, drums, and horns terrified the walled towns, and within two nights they reached Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels captured Chenliu Commandery their ferocious might grew still greater; spears, halberds, drums, and horns terrified the walled towns, and within two nights they reached Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 乘城自墜如雨，故無詖及官吏，盡為賊所虜。

translations.literal: Those who fell from the walls were like rain; thus Wubi and the officials were all captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fell from the walls were like rain; thus Wubi and the officials were all captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊以其將武令珣鎮之。

translations.literal: The rebels appointed their general Wu Lingxun to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels appointed their general Wu Lingxun to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 盧奕

translations.literal: Lu Yi
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi

sentences.zh: 盧奕，黃門監懷慎之少子也。

translations.literal: Lu Yi was the youngest son of Huangmen Supervisor Huaijing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi was the youngest son of Huangmen Supervisor Huaijing.

sentences.zh: 與其兄奐齊名。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Huan were equally renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Huan were equally renowned.

sentences.zh: 大腹豐下，眉目疏朗。

translations.literal: Large-bellied and broad below, with sparse, clear features.
translations.idiomatic: Large-bellied and broad below, with sparse, clear features.

sentences.zh: 謹願寡欲，不尚輿馬，克己自勵。

translations.literal: Cautious and wishing little, he did not esteem carriages and horses, and disciplined himself with effort.
translations.idiomatic: Cautious and wishing little, he did not esteem carriages and horses, and disciplined himself with effort.

sentences.zh: 開元中，任京兆司錄參軍。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he served as registrar of the Jingzhao metropolitan office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era he served as registrar of the Jingzhao metropolitan office.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，為鄠縣令、兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era he was magistrate of Hu County and director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao era he was magistrate of Hu County and director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 所歷有聲，皆如奐之所治也。

translations.literal: Every post he held won acclaim, all like what Huan had governed.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held won acclaim, all like what Huan had governed.

sentences.zh: 天寶八載，轉給事中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao he was transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianbao he was transferred to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 十一載，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he became surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 始懷慎及奐並為中丞，父子三繼，清節不易，時人美之。

translations.literal: At first Huaijing and Huan had both been censors; father and two sons in three generations—integrity unchanged—people praised them.
translations.idiomatic: At first Huaijing and Huan had both been censors; father and two sons in three generations—integrity unchanged—people praised them.

sentences.zh: 奕留臺東都，又分知東都武部選事。

translations.literal: Yi remained at the Eastern Capital court and also shared responsibility for military selection affairs at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yi remained at the Eastern Capital court and also shared responsibility for military selection affairs at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十四載，安祿山犯東都，人吏奔散；

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year An Lushan invaded the Eastern Capital; officials and clerks fled in disorder;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year An Lushan invaded the Eastern Capital; officials and clerks fled in disorder;

sentences.zh: 奕在臺獨居，為賊所執，與李憕同見害。

translations.literal: Yi alone remained in the censorate, was seized by the rebels, and was killed together with Li Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi alone remained in the censorate, was seized by the rebels, and was killed together with Li Cheng.

sentences.zh: 玄宗聞而湣之，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong heard and pitied him, posthumously enfeoffing him as minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong heard and pitied him, posthumously enfeoffing him as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 太常議謚，博士獨孤及議曰：

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated the posthumous title; Academician Dugu Ji argued:
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated the posthumous title; Academician Dugu Ji argued:

sentences.zh: 盧奕剛毅樸忠，直方而清，勵精吏事，所居可紀。

translations.literal: Lu Yi was firm, resolute, plain, and loyal, upright and clear, diligent in administrative affairs—what he governed can be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi was firm, resolute, plain, and loyal, upright and clear, diligent in administrative affairs—what he governed can be recorded.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四載，洛陽陷沒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao Luoyang fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao Luoyang fell.

sentences.zh: 於時東京人士，狼狽鹿駭，猛虎磨牙而爭其肉，居位者皆欲保命而全妻子。

translations.literal: At that time the people of the Eastern Capital were in panic like startled deer; tigers bared fangs to contend for flesh, and those in office all wished to preserve life and keep wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the people of the Eastern Capital were in panic like startled deer; tigers bared fangs to contend for flesh, and those in office all wished to preserve life and keep wives and children.

sentences.zh: 或先策高足，爭脫羿彀；

translations.literal: Some first planned swift escape, striving to slip the archer's bow;
translations.idiomatic: Some first planned swift escape, striving to slip the archer's bow;

sentences.zh: 或不恥茍活，甘飲盜泉。

translations.literal: some were not ashamed to live shamefully, gladly drinking stolen spring water.
translations.idiomatic: some were not ashamed to live shamefully, gladly drinking stolen spring water.

sentences.zh: 奕獨正身守位義不去，以死全節誓不辱。

translations.literal: Yi alone kept upright body and held his post, refusing to leave, swearing death to preserve integrity and not suffer disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Yi alone kept upright body and held his post, refusing to leave, swearing death to preserve integrity and not suffer disgrace.

sentences.zh: 勢窘力屈，以朝服就執，猶慷慨感憤，數賊梟獍之罪。

translations.literal: When his strength was exhausted and he was seized in court dress, he was still ardent and indignant, enumerating the rebels' crimes of ingratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When his strength was exhausted and he was seized in court dress, he was still ardent and indignant, enumerating the rebels' crimes of ingratitude.

sentences.zh: 觀者股栗，奕不變其色，而北面辭君，然後受害。

translations.literal: Onlookers trembled in the legs; Yi did not change color, but faced north to bid farewell to his lord, then suffered harm.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers trembled in the legs; Yi did not change color, but faced north to bid farewell to his lord, then suffered harm.

sentences.zh: 雖古烈士，方之者鮮矣！

translations.literal: Though ancient martyrs—few could match him!
translations.idiomatic: Though ancient martyrs—few could match him!

sentences.zh: 或曰：「洛陽之存亡，操兵者實任其咎，非執法吏所能抗。

translations.literal: Some say: "Whether Luoyang stood or fell, those who wielded troops truly bore the blame—it was not something a law-enforcing clerk could resist.
translations.idiomatic: Some say: "Whether Luoyang stood or fell, those who wielded troops truly bore the blame—it was not something a law-enforcing clerk could resist.

sentences.zh: 師敗將奔，去之可也。

translations.literal: When the army is defeated the general flees—departure was possible.
translations.idiomatic: When the army is defeated the general flees—departure was possible.

sentences.zh: 委身寇仇，以死誰懟？」

translations.literal: To surrender body to the enemy and die—who would be shamed?"
translations.idiomatic: To surrender body to the enemy and die—who would be shamed?"

sentences.zh: 及以為不然。

translations.literal: I consider this wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I consider this wrong.

sentences.zh: 勇者禦而忠者守，必社稷是衛，則死生以之。

translations.literal: The brave defend and the loyal guard; they must protect the altars of soil and grain—life and death follow from this.
translations.idiomatic: The brave defend and the loyal guard; they must protect the altars of soil and grain—life and death follow from this.

sentences.zh: 危而去之，是智免也，於忠何有？

translations.literal: To leave in peril is clever escape—what loyalty is there?
translations.idiomatic: To leave in peril is clever escape—what loyalty is there?

sentences.zh: 昔荀息殺身於晉，不食其言也；

translations.literal: In old days Xun Xi killed himself at Jin, not breaking his word;
translations.idiomatic: In old days Xun Xi killed himself at Jin, not breaking his word;

sentences.zh: 仲由結纓於衛，食焉不避其難也；

translations.literal: Zhong You tied the tassel in Wei, eating his lord's grain and not avoiding hardship;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You tied the tassel in Wei, eating his lord's grain and not avoiding hardship;

sentences.zh: 玄冥勤其官而水死，守位而忘軀也；

translations.literal: Xuanming diligently served his office and died by water, holding post and forgetting body;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanming diligently served his office and died by water, holding post and forgetting body;

sentences.zh: 伯姬待保姆而火死，先禮而後身也。

translations.literal: Lady Bo waited for her nurse and died by fire, putting ritual first and body after.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bo waited for her nurse and died by fire, putting ritual first and body after.

sentences.zh: 彼四人者，死之日，皆於事無補，夫豈愛死而賈禍也！

translations.literal: On the day those four died, it was of no practical help—did they love death and court disaster?
translations.idiomatic: On the day those four died, it was of no practical help—did they love death and court disaster?

sentences.zh: 以為死輕於義，故蹈義而捐生。

translations.literal: They considered death lighter than righteousness, therefore they followed righteousness and cast away life.
translations.idiomatic: They considered death lighter than righteousness, therefore they followed righteousness and cast away life.

sentences.zh: 古史書之，使事君者勸。

translations.literal: Ancient histories recorded it to encourage those who serve lords.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient histories recorded it to encourage those who serve lords.

sentences.zh: 然則祿山之亂，大於裏克、孔悝；

translations.literal: Thus Lushan's disorder was greater than that of Lig Ke and Kong Kui;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Lushan's disorder was greater than that of Lig Ke and Kong Kui;

sentences.zh: 奕廉察之任，切於玄冥之官。

translations.literal: Yi's duty of investigation was more urgent than Xuanming's office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's duty of investigation was more urgent than Xuanming's office.

sentences.zh: 分命所繫，不啻於保姆；

translations.literal: The charge entrusted to him was no less than that of a nurse;
translations.idiomatic: The charge entrusted to him was no less than that of a nurse;

sentences.zh: 逆黨兵威，甚於水火。

translations.literal: the rebel army's might was fiercer than fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: the rebel army's might was fiercer than fire and water.

sentences.zh: 於斯時也，能與執干戈者同其戮力，挽之不來，推之不去，豈不以師可虧，免不可茍，身可殺，節不可奪。

translations.literal: At such a time, able to join those who wielded weapons in shared effort—pull and it would not come, push and it would not go—was it not because the army might be lost but disgrace could not be endured, the body might be killed but integrity could not be seized?
translations.idiomatic: At such a time, able to join those who wielded weapons in shared effort—pull and it would not come, push and it would not go—was it not because the army might be lost but disgrace could not be endured, the body might be killed but integrity could not be seized?

sentences.zh: 故全其特操於白刃之下，孰與夫懷安偷生者同其風哉！

translations.literal: Therefore he preserved his unique integrity beneath white blades—how does that compare in wind with those who cling to ease and steal life!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he preserved his unique integrity beneath white blades—how does that compare in wind with those who cling to ease and steal life!

sentences.zh: 謹按謚法，圖國忘身曰「貞」，秉德遵業曰「烈」。

translations.literal: According to the posthumous-title law, plotting for the state and forgetting body is "Steadfast"; upholding virtue and following enterprise is "Valorous."
translations.idiomatic: According to the posthumous-title law, plotting for the state and forgetting body is "Steadfast"; upholding virtue and following enterprise is "Valorous."

sentences.zh: 奕執憲戎馬之間，志籓王室，可謂圖國；

translations.literal: Yi held the law amid war-horses, his will to shield the royal house—this may be called plotting for the state;
translations.idiomatic: Yi held the law amid war-horses, his will to shield the royal house—this may be called plotting for the state;

sentences.zh: 國危不能拯，而繼之以死，可謂忘身；

translations.literal: when the state was in peril he could not save it and followed with death—this may be called forgetting body;
translations.idiomatic: when the state was in peril he could not save it and followed with death—this may be called forgetting body;

sentences.zh: 歷官一十任，言必正，事必果，而清節不撓，去之若始至，可謂秉德；

translations.literal: through ten offices his words were always upright and deeds decisive, integrity unbent, departing as at first arrival—this may be called upholding virtue;
translations.idiomatic: through ten offices his words were always upright and deeds decisive, integrity unbent, departing as at first arrival—this may be called upholding virtue;

sentences.zh: 先黃門以直道佐時，奕嗣之以忠純，可謂遵業。

translations.literal: the former Huangmen aided the age with the straight Way, and Yi continued with pure loyalty—this may be called following enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: the former Huangmen aided the age with the straight Way, and Yi continued with pure loyalty—this may be called following enterprise.

sentences.zh: 請謚曰「貞烈」。

translations.literal: I request the posthumous title "Steadfast and Valorous."
translations.idiomatic: I request the posthumous title "Steadfast and Valorous."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 蔣清

translations.literal: Jiang Qing
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qing

sentences.zh: 蔣清者，故吏部侍郎欽緒之子。

translations.literal: Jiang Qing was the son of the former Vice Minister of Personnel Qinxu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qing was the son of the former Vice Minister of Personnel Qinxu.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，調補太子校書郎、鞏縣丞，盧奕留之憲府。

translations.literal: Recommended on the Mingjing examination, he was appointed proofreader of the Heir Apparent and vice magistrate of Gong County; Lu Yi retained him in the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended on the Mingjing examination, he was appointed proofreader of the Heir Apparent and vice magistrate of Gong County; Lu Yi retained him in the censorate.

sentences.zh: 清與諸兄溢、演、沇，知名於時。

translations.literal: Qing and his elder brothers Yi, Yan, and Mian were renowned in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and his elder brothers Yi, Yan, and Mian were renowned in their time.

sentences.zh: 奕之被害，清亦死焉。

translations.literal: When Yi was killed, Qing also died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was killed, Qing also died.

sentences.zh: 顏杲卿

translations.literal: Yan Gaoqing
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gaoqing

sentences.zh: 顏杲卿，瑯邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Yan Gaoqing was a native of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gaoqing was a native of Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 世仕江左。

translations.literal: His family served south of the Yangzi for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family served south of the Yangzi for generations.

sentences.zh: 五代祖之推，北齊黃門侍郎、修文館學士。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhitui was vice director of the Huangmen and academician of the Xiuxiang Hall in Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhitui was vice director of the Huangmen and academician of the Xiuxiang Hall in Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊亡入周，始家關內，遂為長安人焉。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou, first settling within the passes, and thus became a man of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered Zhou, first settling within the passes, and thus became a man of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 曾伯祖師古，貞觀中秘書監，自有傳。

translations.literal: His great-great-uncle Shigu, director of the Secretariat in the Zhenguan era, has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-uncle Shigu, director of the Secretariat in the Zhenguan era, has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 曾祖勤禮，崇文館學士。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qinli was academician of the Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qinli was academician of the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 祖甫，曹王侍讀。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fu was reader to the Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fu was reader to the Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 父元孫，垂拱初登進士第，考功員外郎劉奇榜其詞策，文瑰俊拔，多士聳觀。

translations.literal: His father Yuansun passed the jinshi in the early Chuigong era; Examining Affairs Director Liu Qi ranked his policy essay, the writing splendid and outstanding, and the multitude of scholars looked up in awe.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuansun passed the jinshi in the early Chuigong era; Examining Affairs Director Liu Qi ranked his policy essay, the writing splendid and outstanding, and the multitude of scholars looked up in awe.

sentences.zh: 歷官長安尉、太子舍人、亳州刺史卒。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Chang'an, secretary to the Heir Apparent, and prefect of Bozhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as magistrate of Chang'an, secretary to the Heir Apparent, and prefect of Bozhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 杲卿以廕受官，性剛直，有吏幹。

translations.literal: Gaoqing received office by yin privilege; he was stern and upright, with administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing received office by yin privilege; he was stern and upright, with administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為魏州錄事參軍，振舉綱目，政稱第一。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he was registrar of Weizhou, raising standards and regulations; his governance was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era he was registrar of Weizhou, raising standards and regulations; his governance was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四載，攝常山太守。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao he acted as prefect of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao he acted as prefect of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 時安祿山為河北、河東采訪使，常山在其部內。

translations.literal: At that time An Lushan was investigation commissioner of Hebei and Hedong; Changshan lay within his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: At that time An Lushan was investigation commissioner of Hebei and Hedong; Changshan lay within his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，祿山舉范陽之兵詣闕。

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month Lushan raised the army of Fanyang toward the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the eleventh month Lushan raised the army of Fanyang toward the palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月十二日，陷東都。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the twelfth month the Eastern Capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the twelfth month the Eastern Capital fell.

sentences.zh: 杲卿忠誠感發，懼賊遂寇潼關，即危宗社。

translations.literal: Gaoqing, moved by loyalty, feared the rebels would then raid Tong Pass and endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing, moved by loyalty, feared the rebels would then raid Tong Pass and endanger the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 時從弟真卿為平原太守，初聞祿山逆謀，陰養死士，招懷豪右，為拒賊之計。

translations.literal: At that time his cousin Zhenqing was prefect of Pingyuan; having first heard of Lushan's treasonous plot, he secretly trained death-loyal men and won over powerful locals, planning resistance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his cousin Zhenqing was prefect of Pingyuan; having first heard of Lushan's treasonous plot, he secretly trained death-loyal men and won over powerful locals, planning resistance.

sentences.zh: 至是遣使告杲卿，相與起義兵，掎角斷賊歸路，以紓西寇之勢。

translations.literal: Now he sent envoys to inform Gaoqing, and together they raised righteous troops, pincering to cut the rebels' route of return and ease the western invader's pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Now he sent envoys to inform Gaoqing, and together they raised righteous troops, pincering to cut the rebels' route of return and ease the western invader's pressure.

sentences.zh: 杲卿乃與長史袁履謙、前真定令賈深、前內丘丞張通幽等，謀開土門以背之。

translations.literal: Gaoqing then with Chief Clerk Yuan Lüqian, former magistrate of Zhending Jia Shen, former vice magistrate of Neiqiu Zhang Tongyou, and others plotted to open Tumen Pass and strike from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing then with Chief Clerk Yuan Lüqian, former magistrate of Zhending Jia Shen, former vice magistrate of Neiqiu Zhang Tongyou, and others plotted to open Tumen Pass and strike from behind.

sentences.zh: 時祿山遣蔣欽湊、高邈率眾五千守土門。

translations.literal: At that time Lushan dispatched Jiang Qincou and Gao Miao leading five thousand men to hold Tumen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lushan dispatched Jiang Qincou and Gao Miao leading five thousand men to hold Tumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 杲卿欲誅欽湊，開土門之路。

translations.literal: Gaoqing wished to kill Qincou and open the road through Tumen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing wished to kill Qincou and open the road through Tumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 時欽湊軍隸常山郡，屬欽湊遣高邈往幽州未還，杲卿遣吏召欽湊至郡計事。

translations.literal: At that time Qincou's army was subordinate to Changshan Commandery; as Qincou had sent Gao Miao to Youzhou and he had not returned, Gaoqing sent a clerk to summon Qincou to the commandery to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qincou's army was subordinate to Changshan Commandery; as Qincou had sent Gao Miao to Youzhou and he had not returned, Gaoqing sent a clerk to summon Qincou to the commandery to discuss affairs.

sentences.zh: 是月二十二日夜，欽湊至，舍之於傳舍。

translations.literal: That month on the night of the twenty-second Qincou arrived and was lodged at the relay station.
translations.idiomatic: That month on the night of the twenty-second Qincou arrived and was lodged at the relay station.

sentences.zh: 會飲既醉，令袁履謙與參軍馮虔、縣尉李棲默、手力翟萬德等殺欽湊。

translations.literal: When the drinking was finished and he was drunk, Gaoqing ordered Yuan Lüqian and Adjutant Feng Qian, Magistrate Li Qimo, and personal guard Zhai Wande and others to kill Qincou.
translations.idiomatic: When the drinking was finished and he was drunk, Gaoqing ordered Yuan Lüqian and Adjutant Feng Qian, Magistrate Li Qimo, and personal guard Zhai Wande and others to kill Qincou.

sentences.zh: 中夜，履謙以欽湊首見杲卿，相與垂泣，喜事交濟也。

translations.literal: At midnight Lüqian brought Qincou's head to Gaoqing; they wept together, joy and tears mingling.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Lüqian brought Qincou's head to Gaoqing; they wept together, joy and tears mingling.

sentences.zh: 是夜，稾城尉崔安石報高邈還至蒲城，即令馮虔、翟萬德與安石往圖之。

translations.literal: That night Gaocheng Magistrate Cui Anshi reported Gao Miao had returned to Pucheng; Gaoqing immediately ordered Feng Qian, Zhai Wande, and Anshi to go deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: That night Gaocheng Magistrate Cui Anshi reported Gao Miao had returned to Pucheng; Gaoqing immediately ordered Feng Qian, Zhai Wande, and Anshi to go deal with him.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，高邈之騎從數人至稾城驛，安石皆殺之。

translations.literal: At dawn Miao's mounted attendants, a few men, reached Gaocheng Station; Anshi killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Miao's mounted attendants, a few men, reached Gaocheng Station; Anshi killed them all.

sentences.zh: 俄而邈至，安石紿之曰：「太守備酒樂於傳舍。」

translations.literal: Soon Miao arrived; Anshi deceived him, "The prefect has prepared wine and music at the relay station."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Miao arrived; Anshi deceived him, "The prefect has prepared wine and music at the relay station."

sentences.zh: 邈方據廳下馬，馮虔等擒而縶之。

translations.literal: Miao was just dismounting in the hall when Feng Qian and the others seized and bound him.
translations.idiomatic: Miao was just dismounting in the hall when Feng Qian and the others seized and bound him.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊將何千年自東都來趙郡，馮虔、萬德伏兵於醴泉驛，千年至，又擒之。

translations.literal: That day the rebel general He Qiannian came from the Eastern Capital to Zhao Commandery; Feng Qian and Wande lay in ambush at Liquan Station, and when Qiannian arrived they captured him too.
translations.idiomatic: That day the rebel general He Qiannian came from the Eastern Capital to Zhao Commandery; Feng Qian and Wande lay in ambush at Liquan Station, and when Qiannian arrived they captured him too.

sentences.zh: 即日縛二賊將還郡。

translations.literal: That same day they bound the two rebel generals and returned to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That same day they bound the two rebel generals and returned to the commandery.

sentences.zh: 杲卿遣子安平尉泉明及賈深、張通幽、翟萬德，函欽湊之首，械二賊，送於京師。

translations.literal: Gaoqing sent his son Anping Magistrate Quanming with Jia Shen, Zhang Tongyou, and Zhai Wande, bearing Qincou's head in a box and the two rebels in fetters, to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing sent his son Anping Magistrate Quanming with Jia Shen, Zhang Tongyou, and Zhai Wande, bearing Qincou's head in a box and the two rebels in fetters, to the capital.

sentences.zh: 至太原，節度使王承業留泉明、賈深等，寢杲卿之表。

translations.literal: At Taiyuan Military Commissioner Wang Chengye detained Quanming, Jia Shen, and the others and suppressed Gaoqing's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan Military Commissioner Wang Chengye detained Quanming, Jia Shen, and the others and suppressed Gaoqing's memorial.

sentences.zh: 承業自上表獻之，以為己功。

translations.literal: Chengye himself submitted a memorial presenting them, taking the credit.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye himself submitted a memorial presenting them, taking the credit.

sentences.zh: 玄宗不之知，擢拜承業大將軍，牙官獲賞者百數。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong did not know; he promoted Chengye to great general, and a hundred-odd staff officers received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong did not know; he promoted Chengye to great general, and a hundred-odd staff officers received rewards.

sentences.zh: 玄宗尋知杲卿之功，乃加衛尉卿、兼御史大夫，以袁履謙為常山太守，賈深為司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor soon learned of Gaoqing's achievement and further appointed him director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and concurrently censor-in-chief; Yuan Lüqian became prefect of Changshan and Jia Shen army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon learned of Gaoqing's achievement and further appointed him director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and concurrently censor-in-chief; Yuan Lüqian became prefect of Changshan and Jia Shen army marshal.

sentences.zh: 杲卿既斬賊將，收兵練卒，乃檄告河北郡縣，言朝廷以榮王為河北兵馬大元帥，哥舒翰為副，統眾三十萬，即出土門。

translations.literal: After Gaoqing had beheaded the rebel generals and gathered and trained troops, he issued a proclamation to the commanderies of Hebei, stating that the court had appointed Prince of Rong as grand marshal of Hebei military forces and Geshu Han as deputy, commanding three hundred thousand men, about to emerge from Tumen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaoqing had beheaded the rebel generals and gathered and trained troops, he issued a proclamation to the commanderies of Hebei, stating that the court had appointed Prince of Rong as grand marshal of Hebei military forces and Geshu Han as deputy, commanding three hundred thousand men, about to emerge from Tumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 郡縣聞之，皆殺賊守將，遠近響應，時十五郡皆為國家所守。

translations.literal: When the commanderies heard this they all killed rebel garrison commanders; near and far responded, and at the time fifteen commanderies were held for the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the commanderies heard this they all killed rebel garrison commanders; near and far responded, and at the time fifteen commanderies were held for the state.

sentences.zh: 時安祿山遣使傳李憕、盧奕之首徇河北。

translations.literal: At that time An Lushan sent envoys bearing the heads of Li Cheng and Lu Yi through Hebei as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: At that time An Lushan sent envoys bearing the heads of Li Cheng and Lu Yi through Hebei as a warning.

sentences.zh: 至平原，真卿殺賊使，收藏憕等首。

translations.literal: Reaching Pingyuan, Zhenqing killed the rebel envoy and preserved the heads of Cheng and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Pingyuan, Zhenqing killed the rebel envoy and preserved the heads of Cheng and the others.

sentences.zh: 清池尉賈載亦斬偽署景城守劉玄道，傳首於平原。

translations.literal: Qingchi Vice Magistrate Jia Zai also beheaded the falsely appointed garrison commander of Jingcheng Liu Xuandao and sent the head to Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qingchi Vice Magistrate Jia Zai also beheaded the falsely appointed garrison commander of Jingcheng Liu Xuandao and sent the head to Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 饒陽郡守盧全誠亦據郡舉兵，會於真卿。

translations.literal: Raoyang Commandery Administrator Lu Quancheng also held the commandery and raised troops, joining Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: Raoyang Commandery Administrator Lu Quancheng also held the commandery and raised troops, joining Zhenqing.

sentences.zh: 時常山、平原二郡兵威大振。

translations.literal: At that time the military might of Changshan and Pingyuan commanderies greatly swelled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the military might of Changshan and Pingyuan commanderies greatly swelled.

sentences.zh: 祿山方自率眾而西，已至陜，聞河北有變而還，乃命史思明、蔡希德率眾渡河。

translations.literal: Lushan was just leading his forces west and had reached Shan; hearing of changes in Hebei he returned and ordered Shi Siming and Cai Xide to lead forces across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was just leading his forces west and had reached Shan; hearing of changes in Hebei he returned and ordered Shi Siming and Cai Xide to lead forces across the river.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，思明攻常山郡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year Siming attacked Changshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year Siming attacked Changshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 城中兵少，眾寡不敵，禦備皆竭。

translations.literal: Troops in the city were few; they could not match the multitude, and defenses were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Troops in the city were few; they could not match the multitude, and defenses were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 其月八日，城陷，杲卿、履謙為賊所執，送於東都。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of that month the city fell; Gaoqing and Lüqian were seized by the rebels and sent to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of that month the city fell; Gaoqing and Lüqian were seized by the rebels and sent to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 思明既陷常山，遂攻諸郡，鄴、廣平、鉅鹿、趙郡、上谷、博陵、文安、魏郡、信都，復為賊守。

translations.literal: After Siming captured Changshan he attacked the other commanderies; Ye, Guangping, Julu, Zhao, Shanggu, Boling, Wen'an, Wei, and Xindu again became rebel-held.
translations.idiomatic: After Siming captured Changshan he attacked the other commanderies; Ye, Guangping, Julu, Zhao, Shanggu, Boling, Wen'an, Wei, and Xindu again became rebel-held.
