sentences.zh: 祿山見杲卿，面責之曰：「汝昨自范陽戶曹，我奏為判官，遂得光祿、太常二丞，便用汝攝常山太守，負汝何事而背我耶？」

translations.literal: Lushan saw Gaoqing and rebuked him face to face: "You were yesterday a household registrar in Fanyang; I memorialized you as case officer, then gave you director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Grand Temple—then used you as acting prefect of Changshan. What did I owe you that you betrayed me?"
translations.idiomatic: Lushan saw Gaoqing and rebuked him face to face: "You were yesterday a household registrar in Fanyang; I memorialized you as case officer, then gave you director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Grand Temple—then used you as acting prefect of Changshan. What did I owe you that you betrayed me?"

sentences.zh: 杲卿瞋目而報曰：「我世為唐臣，常守忠義，縱受汝奏署，復合從汝反乎！

translations.literal: Gaoqing glared and replied, "My family for generations has been subjects of Tang, ever holding loyalty and righteousness; though I received your memorial appointment, should I have followed you in rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing glared and replied, "My family for generations has been subjects of Tang, ever holding loyalty and righteousness; though I received your memorial appointment, should I have followed you in rebellion?

sentences.zh: 且汝本營州一牧羊羯奴耳，叨竊恩寵，致身及此，天子負汝何事而汝反耶？」

translations.literal: Moreover you were originally a sheep-herding Jie slave of Yingzhou, undeservedly enjoying favor and reaching this height—what did the Son of Heaven owe you that you rebelled?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you were originally a sheep-herding Jie slave of Yingzhou, undeservedly enjoying favor and reaching this height—what did the Son of Heaven owe you that you rebelled?"

sentences.zh: 祿山怒甚，令縛於中橋南頭從西第二柱，節解之，比至氣絕，大罵不息。

translations.literal: Lushan was greatly enraged and ordered him bound at the south end of the central bridge, second pillar from the west, and dismembered limb by limb; until breath stopped he cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was greatly enraged and ordered him bound at the south end of the central bridge, second pillar from the west, and dismembered limb by limb; until breath stopped he cursed without cease.

sentences.zh: 是日杲卿幼子誕、侄詡及袁履謙，皆被先截手足，何千年弟在傍，含血噴其面，因加割臠，路人見之流涕。

translations.literal: That day Gaoqing's young son Dan, nephew Xu, and Yuan Lüqian all had hands and feet cut off first; He Qiannian's younger brother stood by, spraying blood on their faces, then further cutting flesh—passersby wept at the sight.
translations.idiomatic: That day Gaoqing's young son Dan, nephew Xu, and Yuan Lüqian all had hands and feet cut off first; He Qiannian's younger brother stood by, spraying blood on their faces, then further cutting flesh—passersby wept at the sight.

sentences.zh: 其年二月，李光弼、郭子儀之師自土門東下，復收常山郡。

translations.literal: That year in the second month the armies of Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi came down from Tumen Pass east and recaptured Changshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the second month the armies of Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi came down from Tumen Pass east and recaptured Changshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 杲卿、履謙等妻女數百人，繫之獄中，光弼破械出之，令行喪服，給遣周厚。

translations.literal: Several hundred wives and daughters of Gaoqing, Lüqian, and the others were imprisoned; Guangbi broke their fetters, ordered mourning dress, and gave generous support for their departure.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred wives and daughters of Gaoqing, Lüqian, and the others were imprisoned; Guangbi broke their fetters, ordered mourning dress, and gave generous support for their departure.

sentences.zh: 至德二年冬，廣平王收復兩京，史思明以河朔歸國。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Zhide the Prince of Guangping recovered the two capitals; Shi Siming submitted Hebei to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Zhide the Prince of Guangping recovered the two capitals; Shi Siming submitted Hebei to the state.

sentences.zh: 時真卿為蒲州刺史，乃令泉明於河北求訪血屬。

translations.literal: At that time Zhenqing was prefect of Puzhou; he ordered Quanming to seek blood kin in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhenqing was prefect of Puzhou; he ordered Quanming to seek blood kin in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 杲卿妹先適故榆次令張景儋，妹女流落賊中，泉明一女亦落賊中，俱索購錢三萬。

translations.literal: Gaoqing's younger sister had earlier married the former magistrate of Yuci Zhang Jingdan; her daughter was lost among the rebels, and Quanming's daughter also fell among rebels—each required thirty thousand in ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing's younger sister had earlier married the former magistrate of Yuci Zhang Jingdan; her daughter was lost among the rebels, and Quanming's daughter also fell among rebels—each required thirty thousand in ransom.

sentences.zh: 泉明悉索所費，購姑女而還，比復納購，己女遂失。

translations.literal: Quanming spent all he had to buy back his aunt's daughter; when he again paid ransom his own daughter was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Quanming spent all he had to buy back his aunt's daughter; when he again paid ransom his own daughter was lost.

sentences.zh: 而袁履謙已下，父之將吏妻子奴隸三百餘人，轉徙賊中，窮窘無告。

translations.literal: Below Yuan Lüqian, more than three hundred wives, children, slaves, and servants of fathers' generals and officials wandered among rebels, destitute with none to plead.
translations.idiomatic: Below Yuan Lüqian, more than three hundred wives, children, slaves, and servants of fathers' generals and officials wandered among rebels, destitute with none to plead.

sentences.zh: 泉明悉以歸蒲州，真卿贍給久之，隨其所詣而資送之。

translations.literal: Quanming brought them all back to Puzhou; Zhenqing supported them for a long time and sent them on according to their wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Quanming brought them all back to Puzhou; Zhenqing supported them for a long time and sent them on according to their wishes.

sentences.zh: 泉明求其父屍於東都，得其行刑者，言杲卿被害時，先斷一足，與履謙同坎瘞之。

translations.literal: Quanming sought his father's corpse in the Eastern Capital and found the executioner, who said when Gaoqing was killed they first cut off one foot and buried him in the same pit with Lüqian.
translations.idiomatic: Quanming sought his father's corpse in the Eastern Capital and found the executioner, who said when Gaoqing was killed they first cut off one foot and buried him in the same pit with Lüqian.

sentences.zh: 及發瘞得屍，果無一足，即日與履謙之屍，各為一柩，扶護還長安。

translations.literal: When the pit was opened the corpse indeed lacked one foot; that day he and Lüqian's corpse each received a coffin and were escorted back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the pit was opened the corpse indeed lacked one foot; that day he and Lüqian's corpse each received a coffin and were escorted back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 初，履謙妻疑夫柩殮衣儉薄，發棺視之，一與杲卿等，履謙妻號踴感嘆，待之如父。

translations.literal: At first Lüqian's wife suspected her husband's coffin burial clothes were meager; opening the coffin she looked—identical to Gaoqing's—and wailed and stamped, treating him like a father.
translations.idiomatic: At first Lüqian's wife suspected her husband's coffin burial clothes were meager; opening the coffin she looked—identical to Gaoqing's—and wailed and stamped, treating him like a father.

sentences.zh: 泉明之志行仁義如此。

translations.literal: Quanming's will and conduct in benevolence and righteousness were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Quanming's will and conduct in benevolence and righteousness were thus.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年五月，詔曰：「故衛尉卿、兼御史中丞、恆州刺史顏杲卿，任彼專城，志梟狂虜，艱難之際，忠義在心。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Qianyuan an edict said: "The late Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, concurrently surveillance censor and prefect of Hengzhou Yan Gaoqing, holding that walled city alone, resolved to destroy the mad invader; in hardship his loyalty and righteousness were in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Qianyuan an edict said: "The late Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, concurrently surveillance censor and prefect of Hengzhou Yan Gaoqing, holding that walled city alone, resolved to destroy the mad invader; in hardship his loyalty and righteousness were in his heart.

sentences.zh: 憤群兇而慷慨，臨大節而奮發，遂擒元惡，成此茂勛。

translations.literal: Indignant at the multitude of villains he was ardent; facing great integrity he roused himself, and thus captured the chief villain and achieved this splendid merit.
translations.idiomatic: Indignant at the multitude of villains he was ardent; facing great integrity he roused himself, and thus captured the chief villain and achieved this splendid merit.

sentences.zh: 屬胡虜憑陵，流毒方熾，孤城力屈，見陷寇仇，身歿名存，實彰忠烈。

translations.literal: When the barbarian invader relied on force and poison spread fiercely, the lone city exhausted its strength and he fell into the enemy's hands—body perished, name preserved, truly displaying loyal valor.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarian invader relied on force and poison spread fiercely, the lone city exhausted its strength and he fell into the enemy's hands—body perished, name preserved, truly displaying loyal valor.

sentences.zh: 夫仁者有勇，驗之於臨難；

translations.literal: The humane have courage—tested in facing hardship;
translations.idiomatic: The humane have courage—tested in facing hardship;

sentences.zh: 臣之報國，義存於捐軀。

translations.literal: the minister's repayment of the state lies in casting away body.
translations.idiomatic: the minister's repayment of the state lies in casting away body.

sentences.zh: 嘉其死節之誠，未備飾終之禮，可贈太子太保。」

translations.literal: We praise the sincerity of his death in integrity; the rites of honoring the end are not yet complete—he may be posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent."
translations.idiomatic: We praise the sincerity of his death in integrity; the rites of honoring the end are not yet complete—he may be posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent."

sentences.zh: 薛願

translations.literal: Xue Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuan

sentences.zh: 薛願，河東汾陰人。

translations.literal: Xue Yuan was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuan was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父縚，禮部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Tao was director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao was director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 兄崇一，尚惠宣太子女宜君縣主。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chongyi married the Princess of Yijun, daughter of Princess Huixuan.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chongyi married the Princess of Yijun, daughter of Princess Huixuan.

sentences.zh: 女弟為廢太子瑛妃。

translations.literal: A younger sister was consort to the deposed Crown Prince Ying.
translations.idiomatic: A younger sister was consort to the deposed Crown Prince Ying.

sentences.zh: 願坐宮廢貶官。

translations.literal: Yuan was demoted because of the palace affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was demoted because of the palace affair.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，南陽節度使魯炅奏用願為潁川太守、本郡防禦使。

translations.literal: In Lushan's disorder Nanyang Military Commissioner Lu Hui memorialized Yuan as prefect of Yingchuan and defense commissioner of that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Lushan's disorder Nanyang Military Commissioner Lu Hui memorialized Yuan as prefect of Yingchuan and defense commissioner of that commandery.

sentences.zh: 時賊已陷陳留、滎陽、汝南等郡，方圍南陽。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels had already captured Chenliu, Xingyang, Runan, and other commanderies and were besieging Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebels had already captured Chenliu, Xingyang, Runan, and other commanderies and were besieging Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 潁川當其來往之路，願與防禦副使龐堅同力固守，城中儲蓄無素，兵卒單寡。

translations.literal: Yingchuan lay on their route of passage; Yuan and Vice Defense Commissioner Pang Jian together held firm; stores in the city were not prepared beforehand, and soldiers were few.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan lay on their route of passage; Yuan and Vice Defense Commissioner Pang Jian together held firm; stores in the city were not prepared beforehand, and soldiers were few.

sentences.zh: 自至德元年正月至十一月，賊晝夜攻之不息，距城百里，廬舍墳墓林樹開發斬徹殆盡，而外救無至。

translations.literal: From the first month of the first year of Zhide to the eleventh month the rebels attacked day and night without cease; within a hundred li of the city, houses, tombs, groves, and trees were dug up and cut down nearly to nothing, and outside relief did not come.
translations.idiomatic: From the first month of the first year of Zhide to the eleventh month the rebels attacked day and night without cease; within a hundred li of the city, houses, tombs, groves, and trees were dug up and cut down nearly to nothing, and outside relief did not come.

sentences.zh: 賊將阿史那承慶悉以銳卒並攻，為木驢木鵝，雲梯沖棚，四面雲合，鼓噪如雷，矢石如雨，力攻十餘日，城中守備皆竭，賊夜半乘梯而入。

translations.literal: The rebel general Ashina Chengqing attacked with all elite troops together, using wooden rams and wooden geese, scaling ladders and assault sheds; from four sides clouds converged, drums and shouts like thunder, arrows and stones like rain; they pressed the attack for more than ten days until city defenses were exhausted, and at midnight the rebels entered by ladder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Ashina Chengqing attacked with all elite troops together, using wooden rams and wooden geese, scaling ladders and assault sheds; from four sides clouds converged, drums and shouts like thunder, arrows and stones like rain; they pressed the attack for more than ten days until city defenses were exhausted, and at midnight the rebels entered by ladder.

sentences.zh: 願、堅俱被執，送於東都，將支解之。

translations.literal: Yuan and Jian were both seized and sent to the Eastern Capital, about to be dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Jian were both seized and sent to the Eastern Capital, about to be dismembered.

sentences.zh: 或說祿山曰：「薛願、龐堅，義士也。

translations.literal: Someone said to Lushan, "Xue Yuan and Pang Jian are men of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Lushan, "Xue Yuan and Pang Jian are men of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 人各為其主，屠之不祥。」

translations.literal: Each serves his lord; to slaughter them is inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Each serves his lord; to slaughter them is inauspicious."

sentences.zh: 乃繫於洛水之濱，屬苦寒，一夕凍死。

translations.literal: They were then bound on the banks of the Luo; it happened to be bitter cold, and in one night they froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: They were then bound on the banks of the Luo; it happened to be bitter cold, and in one night they froze to death.

sentences.zh: 附 龐堅

translations.literal: Attached: Pang Jian
translations.idiomatic: Attached: Pang Jian

sentences.zh: 堅，武德功臣玉之玄孫。

translations.literal: Jian was the great-grandson of Yu, meritorious minister of the Wude era.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was the great-grandson of Yu, meritorious minister of the Wude era.

sentences.zh: 初娶邠王守禮女建寧縣主。

translations.literal: At first he married Princess Jianning, daughter of Prince of Bin Wang Shouli.
translations.idiomatic: At first he married Princess Jianning, daughter of Prince of Bin Wang Shouli.

sentences.zh: 魯炅奏為潁川郡長史，兼防禦副使。

translations.literal: Lu Hui memorialized him as chief administrator of Yingchuan Commandery and concurrently vice defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hui memorialized him as chief administrator of Yingchuan Commandery and concurrently vice defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 張巡

translations.literal: Zhang Xun
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun

sentences.zh: 張巡，蒲州河東人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 兄曉，開元中監察御史。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xiao, in the Kaiyuan era, was surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xiao, in the Kaiyuan era, was surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆以文行知名。

translations.literal: The brothers were both renowned for literary conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were both renowned for literary conduct.

sentences.zh: 巡聰悟有才幹，舉進士，三以書判拔萃入等。

translations.literal: Xun was intelligent and talented; he passed the jinshi and three times entered the top rank in document judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was intelligent and talented; he passed the jinshi and three times entered the top rank in document judgment.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，調授清河令。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he was appointed magistrate of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he was appointed magistrate of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 有能名，重義尚氣節，人以危窘告者，必傾財以恤之。

translations.literal: He had a reputation for ability, valued righteousness and esteemed integrity; when people told him of distress he would pour out wealth to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: He had a reputation for ability, valued righteousness and esteemed integrity; when people told him of distress he would pour out wealth to aid them.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，巡為真源令。

translations.literal: In Lushan's disorder Xun was magistrate of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Lushan's disorder Xun was magistrate of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 說譙郡太守，令完城，募市人，為拒賊之勢。

translations.literal: He persuaded the prefect of Qiao Commandery to repair the walls, recruit townspeople, and form resistance to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded the prefect of Qiao Commandery to repair the walls, recruit townspeople, and form resistance to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時吳王祗為靈昌太守，奉詔糾率河南諸郡，練兵以拒逆黨，濟南太守李隨副之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Wu Zhi was prefect of Lingchang, ordered to marshal the commanderies of Henan, train troops to resist the rebels, with Prefect of Jinan Li Sui as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince of Wu Zhi was prefect of Lingchang, ordered to marshal the commanderies of Henan, train troops to resist the rebels, with Prefect of Jinan Li Sui as deputy.

sentences.zh: 巡與單父尉賈賁各召募豪傑，同為義舉。

translations.literal: Xun and Danfu Vice Magistrate Jia Ben each recruited heroic men and together made righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Danfu Vice Magistrate Jia Ben each recruited heroic men and together made righteous cause.

sentences.zh: 時雍丘令令狐潮欲以其城降賊，民吏百餘人不從命，潮皆反接，仆之於地，將斬之。

translations.literal: At that time Qiao Commandery Magistrate Linghu Chao wished to surrender the city to the rebels; more than a hundred clerks and people would not obey, and Chao bound them all, threw them to the ground, and was about to behead them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qiao Commandery Magistrate Linghu Chao wished to surrender the city to the rebels; more than a hundred clerks and people would not obey, and Chao bound them all, threw them to the ground, and was about to behead them.

sentences.zh: 會賊來攻城，潮遽出鬥，而反接者自解其縛，閉城門拒潮召賁。

translations.literal: Just then rebels came to attack the city; Chao rushed out to fight, and the bound men freed themselves, closed the city gate, refused Chao, and summoned Ben.
translations.idiomatic: Just then rebels came to attack the city; Chao rushed out to fight, and the bound men freed themselves, closed the city gate, refused Chao, and summoned Ben.

sentences.zh: 賁與巡引眾入雍丘，殺潮妻子，嬰城守備。

translations.literal: Ben and Xun led the multitude into Yongqiu, killed Chao's wife and children, and held the city in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Ben and Xun led the multitude into Yongqiu, killed Chao's wife and children, and held the city in defense.

sentences.zh: 吳王祗承制授賁監察御史。

translations.literal: Prince of Wu by provisional order appointed Ben surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wu by provisional order appointed Ben surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 數日，賊來攻城，賁出鬥而死，巡乃合賁之眾城守。

translations.literal: Within days rebels came to attack the city; Ben went out to fight and died; Xun then combined Ben's forces to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Within days rebels came to attack the city; Ben went out to fight and died; Xun then combined Ben's forces to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 令狐潮引賊將李廷望攻圍累月，賊傷夷大半。

translations.literal: Linghu Chao led rebel general Li Tingwang to attack and besiege for months; rebel casualties were more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chao led rebel general Li Tingwang to attack and besiege for months; rebel casualties were more than half.

sentences.zh: 祿山乃於雍丘北置杞州，築城壘以絕餉路，自是內外隔絕。

translations.literal: Lushan then established Qi Prefecture north of Yongqiu, building walls and ramparts to cut the supply route—thereafter inside and outside were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan then established Qi Prefecture north of Yongqiu, building walls and ramparts to cut the supply route—thereafter inside and outside were cut off.

sentences.zh: 又相持累月，賊鋒轉熾，城中益困。

translations.literal: They faced each other for months more; rebel momentum grew fiercer and hardship in the city increased.
translations.idiomatic: They faced each other for months more; rebel momentum grew fiercer and hardship in the city increased.

sentences.zh: 時許遠為睢陽守，與城父令姚同守睢陽城，賊攻之不下。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Yuan was defender of Suiyang; together with Chengfu Magistrate Yao Tong he held Suiyang city, and the rebels could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xu Yuan was defender of Suiyang; together with Chengfu Magistrate Yao Tong he held Suiyang city, and the rebels could not take it.

sentences.zh: 初祿山陷河洛，許叔冀守靈昌，薛願守潁川，許遠守睢陽，皆城孤無援。

translations.literal: When Lushan first captured the He and Luo, Xu Shuji held Lingchang, Xue Yuan held Yingchuan, and Xu Yuan held Suiyang—all lone cities without relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan first captured the He and Luo, Xu Shuji held Lingchang, Xue Yuan held Yingchuan, and Xu Yuan held Suiyang—all lone cities without relief.

sentences.zh: 願守一年而城陷，督冀一年而自拔，獨睢陽堅守。

translations.literal: Yuan held one year and the city fell; Shuji held one year and broke out alone; only Suiyang held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan held one year and the city fell; Shuji held one year and broke out alone; only Suiyang held firm.

sentences.zh: 賊將尹子奇攻圍經年。

translations.literal: Rebel general Yin Ziqi attacked and besieged for a year.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel general Yin Ziqi attacked and besieged for a year.

sentences.zh: 巡以雍丘小邑，儲備不足，大寇臨之，必難保守，乃列卒結陣詐降，至德二年正月也。

translations.literal: Xun, because Yongqiu was a small town with insufficient stores and a great invader pressing it, could not easily be preserved; he arrayed troops in formation feigning surrender—in the first month of the second year of Zhide.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, because Yongqiu was a small town with insufficient stores and a great invader pressing it, could not easily be preserved; he arrayed troops in formation feigning surrender—in the first month of the second year of Zhide.

sentences.zh: 玄宗聞而壯之，授巡主客郎中、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong heard and admired it; he appointed Xun director in the Ministry of Rites and concurrently surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong heard and admired it; he appointed Xun director in the Ministry of Rites and concurrently surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 尹子奇攻圍既久，城中糧盡，易子而食，析骸而爨，人心危恐，慮將有變。

translations.literal: Yin Ziqi besieged for a long time; grain in the city was exhausted—they exchanged children to eat and split bones to cook; hearts were fearful and dreading mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi besieged for a long time; grain in the city was exhausted—they exchanged children to eat and split bones to cook; hearts were fearful and dreading mutiny.

sentences.zh: 巡乃出其妾，對三軍殺之，以饗軍士。

translations.literal: Xun then brought out his concubine and before the three armies killed her to feed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xun then brought out his concubine and before the three armies killed her to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 曰：「諸公為國家戮力守城，一心無二，經年乏食，忠義不衰。

translations.literal: He said, "You all exert strength for the state holding the city, one heart without division; for a year food has been lacking yet loyalty and righteousness do not fade.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "You all exert strength for the state holding the city, one heart without division; for a year food has been lacking yet loyalty and righteousness do not fade.

sentences.zh: 巡不能自割肌膚，以啖將士，豈可惜此婦，坐視危迫。」

translations.literal: Xun cannot cut his own flesh to feed the generals and soldiers—how can he begrudge this woman and sit watching peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Xun cannot cut his own flesh to feed the generals and soldiers—how can he begrudge this woman and sit watching peril!"

sentences.zh: 將士皆泣下，不忍食，巡強令食之。

translations.literal: Generals and soldiers all wept and could not bear to eat; Xun forced them to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and soldiers all wept and could not bear to eat; Xun forced them to eat.

sentences.zh: 乃括城中婦人；

translations.literal: Then they gathered the women of the city;
translations.idiomatic: Then they gathered the women of the city;

sentences.zh: 既盡，以男夫老小繼之，所食人口二三萬，人心終不離變。

translations.literal: when those were exhausted, men, old and young followed—those eaten numbered twenty or thirty thousand, yet hearts never turned from change.
translations.idiomatic: when those were exhausted, men, old and young followed—those eaten numbered twenty or thirty thousand, yet hearts never turned from change.

sentences.zh: 時賀蘭進明以重兵守臨淮，巡遣帳下之士南霽雲夜縋出城，求援於進明。

translations.literal: At that time Helan Jinming held heavy troops at Linhuai; Xun sent his officer Nan Jiyun to lower himself by rope from the city at night and seek relief from Jinming.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Helan Jinming held heavy troops at Linhuai; Xun sent his officer Nan Jiyun to lower himself by rope from the city at night and seek relief from Jinming.

sentences.zh: 進明日與諸將張樂高會，無出師意。

translations.literal: The next day Jinming feasted the generals with music at a high gathering, with no intention of marching out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jinming feasted the generals with music at a high gathering, with no intention of marching out.

sentences.zh: 霽雲泣告之曰：「本州強寇淩逼，重圍半年，食盡兵窮，計無從出。

translations.literal: Jiyun wept and told him, "Our prefecture is violently pressed by a strong foe; besieged half a year, food exhausted and troops spent—there is no way out.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun wept and told him, "Our prefecture is violently pressed by a strong foe; besieged half a year, food exhausted and troops spent—there is no way out.

sentences.zh: 初圍城之日，城中數萬口，今婦人老幼，相食殆盡，張中丞殺愛妾以啖軍人，今見存之數，不過數千，城中之人，分當餌賊。

translations.literal: When the siege began the city had tens of thousands; now women, old and young, have nearly all been eaten; Vice Censor Zhang killed his beloved concubine to feed the soldiers—those who remain number only a few thousand; the people of the city must in turn become bait for the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege began the city had tens of thousands; now women, old and young, have nearly all been eaten; Vice Censor Zhang killed his beloved concubine to feed the soldiers—those who remain number only a few thousand; the people of the city must in turn become bait for the rebels.

sentences.zh: 但睢陽既拔，即及臨淮，皮毛相依，理須援助。

translations.literal: But once Suiyang falls, it reaches Linhuai; hide and fur depend on each other—aid must by reason be given.
translations.idiomatic: But once Suiyang falls, it reaches Linhuai; hide and fur depend on each other—aid must by reason be given.

sentences.zh: 霽雲所以冒賊鋒刃，匍匐乞師，謂大夫深念危亡，言發響應，何得宴安自處，殊無救恤之心？

translations.literal: Jiyun therefore braved the rebels' blades, crawling to beg troops, thinking the grandee deeply mindful of peril and ruin, that words would ring with response—how can he feast in ease with utterly no heart to save and succor?
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun therefore braved the rebels' blades, crawling to beg troops, thinking the grandee deeply mindful of peril and ruin, that words would ring with response—how can he feast in ease with utterly no heart to save and succor?

sentences.zh: 夫忠臣義士之所為，豈宜如此！

translations.literal: What loyal ministers and righteous men do—should it be thus!
translations.idiomatic: What loyal ministers and righteous men do—should it be thus!

sentences.zh: 霽雲既不能達主將之意，請嚙一指，留於大夫，示之以信，歸報本州。」

translations.literal: Jiyun cannot reach the chief general's intent; I beg to bite off one finger and leave it with the grandee as proof, to report back to our prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun cannot reach the chief general's intent; I beg to bite off one finger and leave it with the grandee as proof, to report back to our prefecture."

sentences.zh: 霽雲自臨淮還睢陽，繩城而入。

translations.literal: Jiyun returned from Linhuai to Suiyang and entered the city by rope.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun returned from Linhuai to Suiyang and entered the city by rope.

sentences.zh: 城中將吏知救不至，慟哭累日。

translations.literal: Generals and officials in the city, knowing relief would not come, wept for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and officials in the city, knowing relief would not come, wept for many days.

sentences.zh: 十月，城陷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the city fell.

sentences.zh: 巡與姚、南霽雲、許遠，皆為賊所執。

translations.literal: Xun, Yao, Nan Jiyun, and Xu Yuan were all seized by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Yao, Nan Jiyun, and Xu Yuan were all seized by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 巡神氣慷慨，每與賊戰，大呼誓師，眥裂血流，齒牙皆碎。

translations.literal: Xun's spirit was ardent; each time he fought the rebels he shouted to rally the army, eyes splitting and blood flowing, teeth all shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's spirit was ardent; each time he fought the rebels he shouted to rally the army, eyes splitting and blood flowing, teeth all shattered.

sentences.zh: 城將陷，西向再拜，曰：「臣智勇俱竭，不能式遏強寇，保守孤城。

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall he bowed twice to the west and said, "Your servant's wisdom and courage are both exhausted; I cannot check the strong foe or preserve this lone city.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall he bowed twice to the west and said, "Your servant's wisdom and courage are both exhausted; I cannot check the strong foe or preserve this lone city.

sentences.zh: 臣雖為鬼，誓與賊為厲，以答明恩。」

translations.literal: Though I become a ghost, I swear to be a bane to the rebels, to repay enlightened grace."
translations.idiomatic: Though I become a ghost, I swear to be a bane to the rebels, to repay enlightened grace."

sentences.zh: 及城陷，尹子奇謂巡曰：「聞君每戰眥裂，嚼齒皆碎，何至此耶？」

translations.literal: When the city fell Yin Ziqi said to Xun, "I hear that in each battle your eyes split and you chew your teeth to shards—how did it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Yin Ziqi said to Xun, "I hear that in each battle your eyes split and you chew your teeth to shards—how did it come to this?"

sentences.zh: 巡曰：「吾欲氣吞逆賊，但力不遂耳！」

translations.literal: Xun said, "I wished to swallow the rebels in spirit—but strength did not suffice!"
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "I wished to swallow the rebels in spirit—but strength did not suffice!"

sentences.zh: 子奇以大刀剔巡口，視其齒，存者不過三數。

translations.literal: Ziqi with a great knife pried open Xun's mouth and looked at his teeth—those remaining were no more than three or four.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqi with a great knife pried open Xun's mouth and looked at his teeth—those remaining were no more than three or four.

sentences.zh: 巡大罵曰：「我為君父義死。

translations.literal: Xun cursed loudly, "I die for lord and father in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Xun cursed loudly, "I die for lord and father in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 爾附逆賊，犬彘也，安能久哉！」

translations.literal: You attach to rebel villains—dogs and swine—you cannot last long!"
translations.idiomatic: You attach to rebel villains—dogs and swine—you cannot last long!"

sentences.zh: 子奇義其言，將禮之，左右曰：「此人守義，必不為我用。

translations.literal: Ziqi respected his words and was about to honor him; attendants said, "This man holds righteousness and surely will not serve us.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqi respected his words and was about to honor him; attendants said, "This man holds righteousness and surely will not serve us.

sentences.zh: 素得士心，不可久留。」

translations.literal: He has always won soldiers' hearts—he cannot be kept long."
translations.idiomatic: He has always won soldiers' hearts—he cannot be kept long."

sentences.zh: 是日，與姚、霽雲同被害，唯許遠執送洛陽。

translations.literal: That day he was killed together with Yao and Jiyun; only Xu Yuan was sent under escort to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That day he was killed together with Yao and Jiyun; only Xu Yuan was sent under escort to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 附 姚誾

translations.literal: Attached: Yao Yin
translations.idiomatic: Attached: Yao Yin

sentences.zh: 姚誾者，浹州平陸人，故相梁國公崇之侄孫。

translations.literal: Yao Yin was a native of Pinglu in Jiazhou, grandnephew of former Chancellor Duke of Liang Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yin was a native of Pinglu in Jiazhou, grandnephew of former Chancellor Duke of Liang Chong.

sentences.zh: 父弇，開元初歷處州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yan, in the early Kaiyuan era, served in succession as prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan, in the early Kaiyuan era, served in succession as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 誾性豪蕩，好飲謔，善絲竹。

translations.literal: Yin was bold and unrestrained, fond of drinking and jest, skilled at stringed music.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was bold and unrestrained, fond of drinking and jest, skilled at stringed music.

sentences.zh: 歷壽安尉、城父令，與張巡素相親善。

translations.literal: He served in succession as vice magistrate of Shou'an and magistrate of Chengfu; he was always close to Zhang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as vice magistrate of Shou'an and magistrate of Chengfu; he was always close to Zhang Xun.

sentences.zh: 以守睢陽之功，至德二年春，加檢校尚書侍郎。

translations.literal: For defending Suiyang he was in the spring of the second year of Zhide further made acting vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For defending Suiyang he was in the spring of the second year of Zhide further made acting vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 賈賁者，故閬州刺史璿之子也。

translations.literal: Jia Ben was the son of the former Prefect of Langzhou Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Ben was the son of the former Prefect of Langzhou Xuan.

sentences.zh: 許遠

translations.literal: Xu Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan

sentences.zh: 許遠者，杭州鹽官人也。

translations.literal: Xu Yuan was a native of Yanguan in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was a native of Yanguan in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 世仕江右。

translations.literal: His family served the lands south of the Yangzi for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family served the lands south of the Yangzi for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖高陽公敬宗，龍朔中宰相，自有傳。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Duke of Gaoyang Jingzong, chancellor in the Longshuo era, has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Duke of Gaoyang Jingzong, chancellor in the Longshuo era, has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 遠清幹，初從軍河西，為磧西支度判官。

translations.literal: Yuan was clear and capable; he first followed the army in Hexi as disbursement case officer of the Western Deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was clear and capable; he first followed the army in Hexi as disbursement case officer of the Western Deserts.

sentences.zh: 章仇兼瓊鎮劍南，又辟為從事。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiu Jianqiong governed Jiannan and also recruited him as staff member.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiu Jianqiong governed Jiannan and also recruited him as staff member.

sentences.zh: 慕其門，欲以子妻之。

translations.literal: Admiring his house, he wished to marry his son to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Admiring his house, he wished to marry his son to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 遠辭，兼瓊怒，積他事中傷，貶為高要尉。

translations.literal: Yuan declined; Jianqiong was angry and accumulated other matters to harm him, demoting him to vice magistrate of Gaoyao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan declined; Jianqiong was angry and accumulated other matters to harm him, demoting him to vice magistrate of Gaoyao.

sentences.zh: 後遇赦得還。

translations.literal: Later he met amnesty and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later he met amnesty and returned.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，不次拔將帥，或薦遠素練戎事。

translations.literal: In Lushan's disorder generals were promoted out of order; some recommended Yuan as long skilled in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Lushan's disorder generals were promoted out of order; some recommended Yuan as long skilled in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 玄宗召見，拜睢陽太守，累加侍御史、本州防禦使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong summoned and saw him, appointing him prefect of Suiyang, cumulatively promoted to attendant censor and defense commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong summoned and saw him, appointing him prefect of Suiyang, cumulatively promoted to attendant censor and defense commissioner of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及賊將尹子奇攻圍，遠與張巡、姚摐嬰城拒守經年，外救不至，兵糧俱盡而城陷。

translations.literal: When rebel general Yin Ziqi attacked and besieged, Yuan with Zhang Xun and Yao Chong held the city for a year; outside relief did not come, troops and grain were both exhausted, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel general Yin Ziqi attacked and besieged, Yuan with Zhang Xun and Yao Chong held the city for a year; outside relief did not come, troops and grain were both exhausted, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 尹子奇執送洛陽，與哥舒翰、程千里，俱囚之客省。

translations.literal: Yin Ziqi seized and sent him to Luoyang, imprisoning him with Geshu Han and Cheng Qianli in the Guest Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi seized and sent him to Luoyang, imprisoning him with Geshu Han and Cheng Qianli in the Guest Bureau.

sentences.zh: 及安慶緒敗，渡河北走，使嚴莊皆害之。

translations.literal: When An Qingxu was defeated and fled north across the river, he ordered Yan Zhuang to kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu was defeated and fled north across the river, he ordered Yan Zhuang to kill them all.

sentences.zh: 初，賀蘭進明與房琯素不相葉。

translations.literal: At first Helan Jinming and Fang Guan had never been on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: At first Helan Jinming and Fang Guan had never been on good terms.

sentences.zh: 及琯為宰相，進明時為御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Guan became chancellor, Jinming was then censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan became chancellor, Jinming was then censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 琯奏用進明為彭城太守、河南節度使、兼御史大夫，代嗣虢王巨；

translations.literal: Guan memorialized Jinming as prefect of Pengcheng, Henan military commissioner, and concurrently censor-in-chief, replacing the Prince of Guo Wang Ju;
translations.idiomatic: Guan memorialized Jinming as prefect of Pengcheng, Henan military commissioner, and concurrently censor-in-chief, replacing the Prince of Guo Wang Ju;

sentences.zh: 復用靈昌太守許叔冀為進明都知兵馬、兼御史大夫，重其官以挫進明。

translations.literal: he again used Lingchang Prefect Xu Shuji as Jinming's director of all military affairs and concurrently censor-in-chief, weighting his office to check Jinming.
translations.idiomatic: he again used Lingchang Prefect Xu Shuji as Jinming's director of all military affairs and concurrently censor-in-chief, weighting his office to check Jinming.

sentences.zh: 虢王巨受代之時，盡將部曲而行，所留者揀退羸兵數千人、劣馬數百匹，不堪扞賊。

translations.literal: When Prince of Guo Wang Ju was replaced he took all his troops and departed, leaving only several thousand picked-over weak soldiers and several hundred inferior horses, unfit to resist rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Guo Wang Ju was replaced he took all his troops and departed, leaving only several thousand picked-over weak soldiers and several hundred inferior horses, unfit to resist rebels.

sentences.zh: 叔冀恃部下精銳，又名位等於進明，自謂匹敵，不受進明節制。

translations.literal: Shuji relied on his troops as elite and his rank as equal to Jinming; he considered himself a match and would not accept Jinming's command.
translations.idiomatic: Shuji relied on his troops as elite and his rank as equal to Jinming; he considered himself a match and would not accept Jinming's command.

sentences.zh: 故南霽雲之乞師，進明不敢分兵，懼叔冀見襲。

translations.literal: Therefore when Nan Jiyun begged troops, Jinming dared not divide forces, fearing Shuji would attack.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when Nan Jiyun begged troops, Jinming dared not divide forces, fearing Shuji would attack.

sentences.zh: 兩相觀望，坐視危亡，致河南郡邑為墟，由執政之乖經制也。

translations.literal: The two watched each other and sat viewing peril and ruin, causing commanderies of Henan to become ruins—from the failure of those in power to govern by constant measure.
translations.idiomatic: The two watched each other and sat viewing peril and ruin, causing commanderies of Henan to become ruins—from the failure of those in power to govern by constant measure.

sentences.zh: 程千里

translations.literal: Cheng Qianli
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qianli

sentences.zh: 程千里，京兆人。

translations.literal: Cheng Qianli was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qianli was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺，骨相魁岸，有勇力。

translations.literal: Seven feet in height, with imposing bone structure, he had courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Seven feet in height, with imposing bone structure, he had courage and strength.

sentences.zh: 本磧西募人，累以戎勛，官至安西副都護。

translations.literal: Originally a recruited man of the Western Deserts, he rose through repeated military merit to vice protector of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Originally a recruited man of the Western Deserts, he rose through repeated military merit to vice protector of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載，授御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao he was appointed surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tianbao he was appointed surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 十二載，兼北庭都護，充安西北庭節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was concurrently protector of Beiting and military commissioner of Anxi and Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was concurrently protector of Beiting and military commissioner of Anxi and Beiting.

sentences.zh: 突厥首領阿布思先率眾內附，隸朔方軍，玄宗賜姓名曰李獻忠。

translations.literal: The Turkic leader Abu Si first led his tribes to submit within the borders and was attached to the Shuofang army; Emperor Xuanzong granted the surname Li and name Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic leader Abu Si first led his tribes to submit within the borders and was attached to the Shuofang army; Emperor Xuanzong granted the surname Li and name Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 李林甫遙領朔方節度，用獻忠為副將。

translations.literal: Li Linfu remotely held the Shuofang commission and used Xianzhong as deputy general.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu remotely held the Shuofang commission and used Xianzhong as deputy general.

sentences.zh: 後有詔移獻忠部落隸幽州，獻忠素與祿山有隙，懼不奉詔，乃叛歸磧北，數為邊患。

translations.literal: Later an edict moved Xianzhong's tribe to Youzhou; Xianzhong had long been at odds with Lushan, feared not to obey the edict, rebelled and returned to the northern deserts, and repeatedly harried the border.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict moved Xianzhong's tribe to Youzhou; Xianzhong had long been at odds with Lushan, feared not to obey the edict, rebelled and returned to the northern deserts, and repeatedly harried the border.

sentences.zh: 玄宗憤之，命千里將兵討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was enraged and ordered Qianli to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong was enraged and ordered Qianli to lead troops against him.

sentences.zh: 十二載十一月，千里兵至磧西，以書喻葛祿，令其相應。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year Qianli's army reached the Western Deserts and wrote to the Geluolu, ordering them to respond in concert.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year Qianli's army reached the Western Deserts and wrote to the Geluolu, ordering them to respond in concert.

sentences.zh: 獻忠勢窮，歸葛祿部。

translations.literal: Xianzhong's strength was exhausted and he returned to the Geluolu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong's strength was exhausted and he returned to the Geluolu tribe.

sentences.zh: 葛祿縛獻忠並其妻子及帳下數千人，送之千里，飛表獻捷，天子壯之。

translations.literal: The Geluolu bound Xianzhong with his wife, children, and several thousand followers under his tent and sent them to Qianli, who flew a memorial announcing victory; the Son of Heaven admired it.
translations.idiomatic: The Geluolu bound Xianzhong with his wife, children, and several thousand followers under his tent and sent them to Qianli, who flew a memorial announcing victory; the Son of Heaven admired it.

sentences.zh: 十三載三月，千里獻俘於勤政樓，斬之於硃雀街，以功授右金吾衛大將軍同正，仍留佐羽林軍。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year Qianli presented captives at Qinzheng Tower; they were beheaded at Zhuque Street, and for merit he was appointed full general of the Right Golden Guard and remained to assist the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year Qianli presented captives at Qinzheng Tower; they were beheaded at Zhuque Street, and for merit he was appointed full general of the Right Golden Guard and remained to assist the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，詔千里於河東召募，充河東節度副使、雲中太守。

translations.literal: In Lushan's disorder an edict ordered Qianli to recruit at Hedong, serving as deputy military commissioner of Hedong and prefect of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Lushan's disorder an edict ordered Qianli to recruit at Hedong, serving as deputy military commissioner of Hedong and prefect of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 十五載正月，遷上黨郡長史、特進，攝御史中丞，以兵守上黨。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year he was transferred to chief administrator of Shangdang Commandery, specially advanced, acting surveillance censor, holding troops to defend Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year he was transferred to chief administrator of Shangdang Commandery, specially advanced, acting surveillance censor, holding troops to defend Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 賊來攻城，屢為千里所敗，以功累加開府儀同三司、禮部尚書、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Rebels came to attack the city and were repeatedly defeated by Qianli; for merit he was cumulatively promoted to honorary grand general and minister of rites and concurrently censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels came to attack the city and were repeatedly defeated by Qianli; for merit he was cumulatively promoted to honorary grand general and minister of rites and concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 至德二年九月，賊將蔡希德圍城，數以輕騎挑戰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Zhide rebel general Cai Xide besieged the city and repeatedly challenged with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Zhide rebel general Cai Xide besieged the city and repeatedly challenged with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 千里恃其驍果，開懸門，率百騎，欲生擒希德。

translations.literal: Qianli relied on his fierce valor, opened the suspended gate, led a hundred horsemen, and wished to capture Xide alive.
translations.idiomatic: Qianli relied on his fierce valor, opened the suspended gate, led a hundred horsemen, and wished to capture Xide alive.

sentences.zh: 勁騎搏之，垂將擒而希德救兵至，千里斂騎而退，橋壞墜坑，反為希德所執。

translations.literal: Strong riders grappled with him; he was just about to seize Xide when Xide's rescue troops arrived; Qianli gathered his horses and withdrew, the bridge broke and he fell into a pit, and was instead seized by Xide.
translations.idiomatic: Strong riders grappled with him; he was just about to seize Xide when Xide's rescue troops arrived; Qianli gathered his horses and withdrew, the bridge broke and he fell into a pit, and was instead seized by Xide.

sentences.zh: 仰首告諸騎曰：「非吾戰之過，此天也！

translations.literal: He raised his head and told the horsemen, "It is not my fault in battle—this is Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: He raised his head and told the horsemen, "It is not my fault in battle—this is Heaven!

sentences.zh: 為我報諸將士，乍可失帥，不可失城。」

translations.literal: Report to the generals and soldiers: better to lose the commander than lose the city."
translations.idiomatic: Report to the generals and soldiers: better to lose the commander than lose the city."

sentences.zh: 軍人聞之泣下，晝夜嚴兵城守，賊竟不能拔。

translations.literal: Soldiers heard and wept; day and night they strictly manned the city, and the rebels ultimately could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers heard and wept; day and night they strictly manned the city, and the rebels ultimately could not take it.

sentences.zh: 千里至東都，安慶緒舍之，偽署特進，囚之客省。

translations.literal: Qianli reached the Eastern Capital; An Qingxu lodged him and falsely appointed him specially advanced, imprisoning him in the Guest Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Qianli reached the Eastern Capital; An Qingxu lodged him and falsely appointed him specially advanced, imprisoning him in the Guest Bureau.

sentences.zh: 及慶緒敗走，為嚴莊所害。

translations.literal: When Qingxu was defeated and fled, Yan Zhuang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingxu was defeated and fled, Yan Zhuang killed him.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，上御丹鳳樓大赦，節文曰：「忠臣事君，有死無貳；

translations.literal: That year in the twelfth month the emperor faced Danfeng Tower for a great amnesty; the text said: "Loyal ministers serve their lord—there is death but no disloyalty;
translations.idiomatic: That year in the twelfth month the emperor faced Danfeng Tower for a great amnesty; the text said: "Loyal ministers serve their lord—there is death but no disloyalty;

sentences.zh: 烈士徇義，雖歿如存。

translations.literal: martyr-scholars follow righteousness—though perished, as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: martyr-scholars follow righteousness—though perished, as if alive.

sentences.zh: 其李憕、盧奕、袁履謙、張巡、許遠、張介然、蔣清、龐堅等，即與追贈，訪其子孫，厚其官爵，家口深加優恤。」

translations.literal: Li Cheng, Lu Yi, Yuan Lüqian, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, Zhang Jieran, Jiang Qing, Pang Jian, and the others shall at once receive posthumous enfeoffment; their descendants shall be sought out, offices and ranks enriched, and households deeply favored and comforted."
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng, Lu Yi, Yuan Lüqian, Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan, Zhang Jieran, Jiang Qing, Pang Jian, and the others shall at once receive posthumous enfeoffment; their descendants shall be sought out, offices and ranks enriched, and households deeply favored and comforted."

sentences.zh: 自是赦恩，無不該於節義，而程千里終以生執賊庭，不霑褒贈。

translations.literal: From then on amnesty grace never failed to cover those of integrity, yet Cheng Qianli ultimately because he was captured alive in the rebel court received no enfeoffment or reward.
translations.idiomatic: From then on amnesty grace never failed to cover those of integrity, yet Cheng Qianli ultimately because he was captured alive in the rebel court received no enfeoffment or reward.

sentences.zh: 袁光庭

translations.literal: Yuan Guangting
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Guangting

sentences.zh: 袁光庭者，河西戍將，天寶末為伊州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan Guangting was a garrison general of Hexi; at the end of Tianbao he was prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Guangting was a garrison general of Hexi; at the end of Tianbao he was prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，西北邊戎兵入赴難，河、隴郡邑，皆為吐蕃所拔。

translations.literal: In Lushan's disorder northwestern border troops entered to aid the crisis; commanderies of He and Long were all captured by Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In Lushan's disorder northwestern border troops entered to aid the crisis; commanderies of He and Long were all captured by Tibet.

sentences.zh: 唯光庭守伊州累年，外救不至。

translations.literal: Only Guangting held Yizhou for years; outside relief did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Only Guangting held Yizhou for years; outside relief did not come.

sentences.zh: 虜百端誘說，終不之屈，部下如一。

translations.literal: The enemy used every means to entice and persuade, yet he never yielded; subordinates were as one.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy used every means to entice and persuade, yet he never yielded; subordinates were as one.

sentences.zh: 及矢石既盡，糧儲並竭，城將陷沒，光庭手殺其妻子，自焚而死。

translations.literal: When arrows and stones were exhausted and grain stores depleted, as the city was about to fall Guangting personally killed his wife and children and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: When arrows and stones were exhausted and grain stores depleted, as the city was about to fall Guangting personally killed his wife and children and burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: The court heard and posthumously enfeoffed him as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: The court heard and posthumously enfeoffed him as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 邵真

translations.literal: Shao Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Shao Zhen

sentences.zh: 邵真者，恆州節度使李寶臣之判官也。

translations.literal: Shao Zhen was case officer to Hengzhou Military Commissioner Li Baochen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Zhen was case officer to Hengzhou Military Commissioner Li Baochen.

sentences.zh: 累加檢校司封郎中、兼御史中丞，專掌文翰，寶臣深所信任。

translations.literal: Cumulatively promoted to acting director in the Ministry of Appointments and concurrently surveillance censor, he exclusively managed documents and was deeply trusted by Baochen.
translations.idiomatic: Cumulatively promoted to acting director in the Ministry of Appointments and concurrently surveillance censor, he exclusively managed documents and was deeply trusted by Baochen.

sentences.zh: 寶臣死，其子惟嶽擅領父眾。

translations.literal: When Baochen died his son Weiyue usurped command of his father's forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Baochen died his son Weiyue usurped command of his father's forces.

sentences.zh: 李正己、田悅遣人說惟嶽同叛，真泣諫曰：「先公位兼將相，受國厚恩，大夫缞绖之中，遽欲違命，同鄰道之惡，違先公之志，必不可也！

translations.literal: Li Zhengyi and Tian Yue sent men to persuade Weiyue to rebel together; Zhen wept and remonstrated, "Our lord held both general and minister rank and received the state's thick grace; the young master, in the midst of mourning garments, suddenly wishes to disobey orders and join the wickedness of neighboring circuits—going against our lord's will—this absolutely cannot be done!
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengyi and Tian Yue sent men to persuade Weiyue to rebel together; Zhen wept and remonstrated, "Our lord held both general and minister rank and received the state's thick grace; the young master, in the midst of mourning garments, suddenly wishes to disobey orders and join the wickedness of neighboring circuits—going against our lord's will—this absolutely cannot be done!

sentences.zh: 田悅與我密邇，絕之又恐速禍；

translations.literal: Tian Yue is close to us; to break with him I fear swift disaster;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue is close to us; to break with him I fear swift disaster;

sentences.zh: 正己稍遠，絕之易耳。

translations.literal: Zhengyi is somewhat distant—breaking with him is easier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyi is somewhat distant—breaking with him is easier.

sentences.zh: 但令悅使還報，請徐思其宜；

translations.literal: Only let Yue's envoy return report and ask to consider the matter slowly;
translations.idiomatic: Only let Yue's envoy return report and ask to consider the matter slowly;

sentences.zh: 執正己使送京師，因請致討，朝廷必嘉大夫之忠，而旌節可得。」

translations.literal: seize Zhengyi's envoy and send him to the capital, then request punitive action—the court will surely praise the young master's loyalty and the command baton may be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: seize Zhengyi's envoy and send him to the capital, then request punitive action—the court will surely praise the young master's loyalty and the command baton may be obtained."

sentences.zh: 惟嶽然之，令真草奏。

translations.literal: Weiyue agreed and ordered Zhen to draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue agreed and ordered Zhen to draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 將發，孔目吏胡震謂惟嶽曰：「此事非細，請與將吏會議。」

translations.literal: As it was about to be sent, clerical officer Hu Zhen said to Weiyue, "This matter is not minor—please discuss with generals and officials."
translations.idiomatic: As it was about to be sent, clerical officer Hu Zhen said to Weiyue, "This matter is not minor—please discuss with generals and officials."

sentences.zh: 長史畢華曰：「先公與二道親好，二十餘年，一朝背之，伏恐生事。

translations.literal: Chief administrator Bi Hua said, "Our lord was on intimate terms with the two circuits for more than twenty years; to turn against them in a morning—I fear trouble will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Bi Hua said, "Our lord was on intimate terms with the two circuits for more than twenty years; to turn against them in a morning—I fear trouble will arise.

sentences.zh: 今執其來使，送於京師，大善。

translations.literal: Now to seize their coming envoy and send him to the capital is very good.
translations.idiomatic: Now to seize their coming envoy and send him to the capital is very good.

sentences.zh: 脫未為朝廷所信，正己兵強，忽來襲城，孤軍無援，何以敵之？

translations.literal: If the court does not yet trust us and Zhengyi's troops are strong, suddenly coming to raid the city—a lone army without relief—how can we resist?
translations.idiomatic: If the court does not yet trust us and Zhengyi's troops are strong, suddenly coming to raid the city—a lone army without relief—how can we resist?

sentences.zh: 不若仍舊勿絕，徐觀其變。」

translations.literal: Better to continue as before without breaking off, and slowly watch for change."
translations.idiomatic: Better to continue as before without breaking off, and slowly watch for change."

sentences.zh: 惟嶽又從之。

translations.literal: Weiyue again followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue again followed this.

sentences.zh: 真又勸惟嶽遣其弟惟簡入朝，仍遣軍吏薛廣嗣詣河東節度馬燧軍求保薦。

translations.literal: Zhen again urged Weiyue to send his younger brother Weijian to court and also send army officer Xue Guangsi to Hedong Military Commissioner Ma Sui's army to seek protection and recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen again urged Weiyue to send his younger brother Weijian to court and also send army officer Xue Guangsi to Hedong Military Commissioner Ma Sui's army to seek protection and recommendation.

sentences.zh: 田悅屯兵束鹿，聞其謀，遣人謂惟嶽曰：「邵真惑亂軍政，必速殺之。

translations.literal: Tian Yue stationed troops at Shulu; hearing of the plot he sent men to tell Weiyue, "Shao Zhen is disturbing military government—you must quickly kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue stationed troops at Shulu; hearing of the plot he sent men to tell Weiyue, "Shao Zhen is disturbing military government—you must quickly kill him.

sentences.zh: 不然，吾且討其罪矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise I shall punish his crime."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I shall punish his crime."

sentences.zh: 惟嶽懼，遂殺真。

translations.literal: Weiyue feared and then killed Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue feared and then killed Zhen.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞而嘉之，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: The court heard and praised him, posthumously enfeoffing Zhen as minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The court heard and praised him, posthumously enfeoffing Zhen as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 符璘

translations.literal: Fu Lin
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lin

sentences.zh: 符璘者，田悅之將。

translations.literal: Fu Lin was a general of Tian Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lin was a general of Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 初，馬燧、李抱真、李芃等破田悅於洹水，燧等進屯魏州。

translations.literal: At first Ma Sui, Li Baozhen, and Li Qi and others defeated Tian Yue at Huan River; Sui and the others advanced and encamped at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ma Sui, Li Baozhen, and Li Qi and others defeated Tian Yue at Huan River; Sui and the others advanced and encamped at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 時悅與李納會於濮陽，因請助兵，納分麾下數千人隨之。

translations.literal: At that time Yue and Li Na met at Puyang and requested aid troops; Na divided several thousand men from his command to follow.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yue and Li Na met at Puyang and requested aid troops; Na divided several thousand men from his command to follow.

sentences.zh: 至是納為河南諸軍所逼，自濮陽奔歸濮州，征兵於悅，悅遣璘將三百騎護送之。

translations.literal: Now Na was pressed by the armies of Henan, fled from Puyang back to Puzhou, and demanded troops from Yue; Yue sent Lin with three hundred horsemen to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: Now Na was pressed by the armies of Henan, fled from Puyang back to Puzhou, and demanded troops from Yue; Yue sent Lin with three hundred horsemen to escort them.

sentences.zh: 納兵既歸，遂悉其眾降於燧。

translations.literal: Once Na's troops returned they all with their forces submitted to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Once Na's troops returned they all with their forces submitted to Sui.

sentences.zh: 遷璘試太子詹事、兼御史中丞，封義陽郡王，實封一百戶。

translations.literal: Lin was transferred to acting mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently surveillance censor, enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang with a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was transferred to acting mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently surveillance censor, enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang with a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 璘父令奇，初為悅部將，至是因璘之出，遂令三子同降於燧。

translations.literal: Lin's father Lingqi had originally been Yue's subordinate general; now because of Lin's departure he ordered his three sons to submit together to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's father Lingqi had originally been Yue's subordinate general; now because of Lin's departure he ordered his three sons to submit together to Sui.

sentences.zh: 悅怒，執令奇，令奇大呼慢罵之，悅族其家。

translations.literal: Yue was enraged, seized Lingqi; Lingqi shouted and reviled him, and Yue exterminated his family.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was enraged, seized Lingqi; Lingqi shouted and reviled him, and Yue exterminated his family.

sentences.zh: 贈令奇戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Lingqi was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Lingqi was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 趙曄

translations.literal: Zhao Ye
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ye

sentences.zh: 趙曄，字雲卿，鄧州穰人，其先自天水徙焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Ye, styled Yunqing, was a native of Rang in Dengzhou; his ancestors had moved there from Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ye, styled Yunqing, was a native of Rang in Dengzhou; his ancestors had moved there from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，主客員外郎德言曾孫也。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was great-grandson of Director of Guests Dezhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era he was great-grandson of Director of Guests Dezhi.

sentences.zh: 父敬先，殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Jingxian was attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingxian was attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 曄志學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Ye aspired to learning and was skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Ye aspired to learning and was skilled at composition.

sentences.zh: 開元中，舉進士，連擢科第，補太子正字，累授大理評事，貶北陽尉，移雷澤、河東二丞。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi, continuously rose in examination rank, was appointed proofreader of the Heir Apparent, cumulatively received the post of reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, was demoted to vice magistrate of Beiyang, and transferred to vice magistrate of Leize and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi, continuously rose in examination rank, was appointed proofreader of the Heir Apparent, cumulatively received the post of reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, was demoted to vice magistrate of Beiyang, and transferred to vice magistrate of Leize and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 河東采訪使韋陟以曄履操清直，頗推敬之，表為賓僚。

translations.literal: Hedong Investigation Commissioner Wei Zhi, because Ye's conduct was pure and upright, greatly respected him and memorialized him as staff member.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong Investigation Commissioner Wei Zhi, because Ye's conduct was pure and upright, greatly respected him and memorialized him as staff member.

sentences.zh: 陟罷，陳留采訪使郭納復奏曄為支使。

translations.literal: When Zhi left office, Chenliu Investigation Commissioner Guo Na again memorialized Ye as branch officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi left office, Chenliu Investigation Commissioner Guo Na again memorialized Ye as branch officer.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山陷陳留，因沒於賊。

translations.literal: When An Lushan captured Chenliu he was thereby lost to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan captured Chenliu he was thereby lost to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時有京兆韋氏，夫任畿官，以不供賊軍遇害，韋被逆賊沒入為婢。

translations.literal: At that time there was a woman of the Wei clan of Jingzhao; her husband held a capital-district office and was killed for not supplying the rebel army; Wei was seized by the rebels and made a servant girl.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a woman of the Wei clan of Jingzhao; her husband held a capital-district office and was killed for not supplying the rebel army; Wei was seized by the rebels and made a servant girl.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使韋儇，族兄弟也。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Observation Commissioner Wei Yi was a clansman.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Observation Commissioner Wei Yi was a clansman.

sentences.zh: 曄哀其冤抑，以錢贖之，俾其妻置之別院，厚供衣食，而曄竟不面其人。

translations.literal: Ye pitied her wrongful oppression, redeemed her with money, had her wife place her in a separate courtyard with generous food and clothing—and Ye never once faced her in person.
translations.idiomatic: Ye pitied her wrongful oppression, redeemed her with money, had her wife place her in a separate courtyard with generous food and clothing—and Ye never once faced her in person.

sentences.zh: 明年，收復東都，曄以家財資給，而訪其親屬歸之，識者咸重焉。

translations.literal: The next year the Eastern Capital was recovered; Ye used family wealth to support her and sought her kin to return her—those who knew all respected this.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Eastern Capital was recovered; Ye used family wealth to support her and sought her kin to return her—those who knew all respected this.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，三司議罪，貶晉江尉。

translations.literal: In the early Qianyuan era the Three Offices deliberated crimes and demoted him to vice magistrate of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianyuan era the Three Offices deliberated crimes and demoted him to vice magistrate of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 數年，改錄事參軍。

translations.literal: After several years he was changed to recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was changed to recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 征拜左補闕，未至。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Remonstrance Official but did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Left Remonstrance Official but did not arrive.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使李承昭奏為判官，授試大理司直、兼監察御史。

translations.literal: Fujian Observation Commissioner Li Chengzhao memorialized him as case officer, appointing him acting chief judge in the Court of Judicial Review and concurrently surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian Observation Commissioner Li Chengzhao memorialized him as case officer, appointing him acting chief judge in the Court of Judicial Review and concurrently surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 試司議郎、兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Acting director in the Court of Advisory Opinion and concurrently attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Acting director in the Court of Advisory Opinion and concurrently attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 入為膳部、比部二員外，膳部、倉部二郎中，秘書少監。

translations.literal: He entered court as director in the Ministries of Provisions and Revenue, director in the Ministries of Provisions and Granaries, and vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as director in the Ministries of Provisions and Revenue, director in the Ministries of Provisions and Granaries, and vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曄性孝悌，敦重交友，雖經艱危，不改其操。

translations.literal: Ye was by nature filial and brotherly, earnest in honoring friendship; though he passed through hardship he did not change his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was by nature filial and brotherly, earnest in honoring friendship; though he passed through hardship he did not change his conduct.

sentences.zh: 少時與殷寅、顏真卿、柳芳、陸據、蕭穎士、李華、邵軫、同志友善，故天寶中語曰：「殷、顏、柳、陸、蕭、李、邵、趙」，以其重行義，敦交道也。

translations.literal: In youth he was close friends with Yin Yin, Yan Zhenqing, Liu Fang, Lu Ju, Xiao Yingshi, Li Hua, and Shao Zhen; thus in the Tianbao era people said, "Yin, Yan, Liu, Lu, Xiao, Li, Shao, Zhao"—for they valued conduct and were earnest in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was close friends with Yin Yin, Yan Zhenqing, Liu Fang, Lu Ju, Xiao Yingshi, Li Hua, and Shao Zhen; thus in the Tianbao era people said, "Yin, Yan, Liu, Lu, Xiao, Li, Shao, Zhao"—for they valued conduct and were earnest in friendship.

sentences.zh: 而曄早擅高名，在宦途五十年，累經貶謫，蹇躓備至。

translations.literal: Yet Ye early won high fame; on the official path for fifty years he was repeatedly demoted, stumbling to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ye early won high fame; on the official path for fifty years he was repeatedly demoted, stumbling to the full.

sentences.zh: 入仕三十年，方霑省官，身在郎署，子常徒步。

translations.literal: Thirty years in office before he touched a central-office post; though in director rank his son often went on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years in office before he touched a central-office post; though in director rank his son often went on foot.

sentences.zh: 官既散曹，俸祿單寡，衣食不充，以至亡歿，服名檢者為之嘆息。

translations.literal: His office was a scattered bureau, salary meager, food and clothing insufficient—until death; those who esteem reputation sighed for him.
translations.idiomatic: His office was a scattered bureau, salary meager, food and clothing insufficient—until death; those who esteem reputation sighed for him.

sentences.zh: 建中四年冬，涇原兵叛，曄竄於山谷。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Jianzhong the Jingyuan troops rebelled; Ye hid in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourth year of Jianzhong the Jingyuan troops rebelled; Ye hid in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾終，追贈華州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness and was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died of illness and was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 子宗儒，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Zongru has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongru has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 石演芬

translations.literal: Shi Yanfen
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanfen

sentences.zh: 石演芬，本西城胡人也。

translations.literal: Shi Yanfen was originally a Hu man of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanfen was originally a Hu man of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 以武勇為朔方邠寧節度兵馬使、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: For martial valor he was military horse commissioner of the Shuofang Binning commission and concurrently censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For martial valor he was military horse commissioner of the Shuofang Binning commission and concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 李懷光養為子，累至右武鋒都將。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang adopted him as son; he rose to commander of the Right Martial Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang adopted him as son; he rose to commander of the Right Martial Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 時懷光軍屯三橋，將與硃泚通謀。

translations.literal: At that time Huaiguang's army was encamped at Sanqiao and was about to conspire with Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huaiguang's army was encamped at Sanqiao and was about to conspire with Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 演芬乃使門客郜成義密疏，具言懷光無狀，請罷其總統。

translations.literal: Yanfen then had his retainer Gao Chengyi secretly memorialize, fully stating Huaiguang's misconduct and requesting removal from overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfen then had his retainer Gao Chengyi secretly memorialize, fully stating Huaiguang's misconduct and requesting removal from overall command.

sentences.zh: 成義至奉天，乃反以其言告懷光子琟，琟密告其父。

translations.literal: Chengyi reached Fengtian and instead reported his words to Huaiguang's son Wei; Wei secretly told his father.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyi reached Fengtian and instead reported his words to Huaiguang's son Wei; Wei secretly told his father.

sentences.zh: 懷光乃召演芬責之曰：「以爾為子，奈何欲破我家！

translations.literal: Huaiguang then summoned Yanfen and rebuked him: "I took you as son—how dare you wish to destroy my house!
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang then summoned Yanfen and rebuked him: "I took you as son—how dare you wish to destroy my house!

sentences.zh: 今死可乎？」

translations.literal: Now will you die?"
translations.idiomatic: Now will you die?"

sentences.zh: 演芬對曰：「天子以公為腹心，公上負天子，安可責演芬！

translations.literal: Yanfen replied, "The Son of Heaven took you as his trusted core—you betray the Son of Heaven; how can you blame Yanfen!
translations.idiomatic: Yanfen replied, "The Son of Heaven took you as his trusted core—you betray the Son of Heaven; how can you blame Yanfen!

sentences.zh: 且演芬胡人，不解異心，欲守事一人，幸免呼為賊。

translations.literal: Moreover Yanfen is a Hu man and does not understand divided loyalty; he wishes to serve one man alone and by luck escape being called a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yanfen is a Hu man and does not understand divided loyalty; he wishes to serve one man alone and by luck escape being called a rebel.

sentences.zh: 死，常分也！」

translations.literal: Death is one's portion!"
translations.idiomatic: Death is one's portion!"

sentences.zh: 懷光使左右臠食之，皆曰：「此忠烈士也！

translations.literal: Huaiguang ordered attendants to cut him to pieces; all said, "This is a loyal martyr!
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang ordered attendants to cut him to pieces; all said, "This is a loyal martyr!

sentences.zh: 可令速死。」

translations.literal: Let him die quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Let him die quickly."

sentences.zh: 乃以刀斷其頸。

translations.literal: They then severed his neck with a blade.
translations.idiomatic: They then severed his neck with a blade.

sentences.zh: 德宗追思義烈，贈兵部尚書，仍賜錢三百千。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong recalled his righteous valor and posthumously enfeoffed him as minister of war, further granting three hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong recalled his righteous valor and posthumously enfeoffed him as minister of war, further granting three hundred thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 又捕得郜成義於朔方，戮之。

translations.literal: Gao Chengyi was also captured in Shuofang and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chengyi was also captured in Shuofang and executed.

sentences.zh: 附 張名振

translations.literal: Attached: Zhang Mingzhen
translations.idiomatic: Attached: Zhang Mingzhen

sentences.zh: 先是，詔賜懷光鐵券。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had bestowed an iron tally on Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had bestowed an iron tally on Huaiguang.

sentences.zh: 懷光奉詔倨慢，左都將張名振大呼軍門曰：「太尉見賊不擊，天使到不迎，固將反耶！

translations.literal: Huaiguang received the edict arrogantly and disrespectfully; Left Commander Zhang Mingzhen shouted at the army gate, "The Grand Marshal sees rebels and does not strike; when the imperial envoy arrives he does not welcome—surely he intends to rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang received the edict arrogantly and disrespectfully; Left Commander Zhang Mingzhen shouted at the army gate, "The Grand Marshal sees rebels and does not strike; when the imperial envoy arrives he does not welcome—surely he intends to rebel!

sentences.zh: 且安史兩賊，僕固懷恩，今皆族滅，公欲何為？

translations.literal: Moreover the two villains An and Shi, and Pugu Huairen—now all their clans are exterminated; what do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the two villains An and Shi, and Pugu Huairen—now all their clans are exterminated; what do you intend?

sentences.zh: 是資忠義之士立功勛耳！」

translations.literal: This only supplies righteous and loyal men to achieve merit and honor!"
translations.idiomatic: This only supplies righteous and loyal men to achieve merit and honor!"

sentences.zh: 懷光聞之，召謂曰：「我不反，為賊強盛，須蓄銳俟時耳。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang heard and summoned him, saying, "I do not rebel; the rebels are too strong—I must store sharpness and await the time."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang heard and summoned him, saying, "I do not rebel; the rebels are too strong—I must store sharpness and await the time."

sentences.zh: 無幾，懷光引軍入咸陽，名振曰：「公乃言不反，今此來何也？

translations.literal: Before long Huaiguang led his army into Xianyang; Mingzhen said, "You said you would not rebel—what is this coming for?
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huaiguang led his army into Xianyang; Mingzhen said, "You said you would not rebel—what is this coming for?

sentences.zh: 何不急攻硃泚，收復京城，以圖富貴？」

translations.literal: Why not hurry to attack Zhu Ci, recover the capital, and seek wealth and honor?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not hurry to attack Zhu Ci, recover the capital, and seek wealth and honor?"

sentences.zh: 懷光曰：「名振病狂。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang said, "Mingzhen is mad with illness."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang said, "Mingzhen is mad with illness."

sentences.zh: 使左右殺之。

translations.literal: He ordered attendants to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered attendants to kill him.

sentences.zh: 張伾

translations.literal: Zhang Pi
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pi

sentences.zh: 張伾，建中初，以澤潞將鎮臨洺。

translations.literal: Zhang Pi, in the early Jianzhong era, as a Ze-Lu general garrisoned Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pi, in the early Jianzhong era, as a Ze-Lu general garrisoned Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 田悅攻之，伾度兵力不能出戰，嚴設守備，嬰城拒守，賊不能拔。

translations.literal: Tian Yue attacked; Pi judged his strength insufficient to sortie, strictly set defenses, held the city and refused surrender—the rebels could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue attacked; Pi judged his strength insufficient to sortie, strictly set defenses, held the city and refused surrender—the rebels could not take it.

sentences.zh: 累月，攻之益急，士多死傷，糧儲漸乏，救兵未至。

translations.literal: Month after month the attack grew fiercer; many soldiers died or were wounded, stores gradually failed, and relief troops did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Month after month the attack grew fiercer; many soldiers died or were wounded, stores gradually failed, and relief troops did not come.

sentences.zh: 伾知事不濟，無以激士心，乃悉召將卒於軍門，命其女出拜之，謂曰：「將士辛苦守戰，伾之家無尺寸物與公等，獨有此女，幸未嫁人，願出賣之，為將士一日之費。」

translations.literal: Pi knew affairs would not succeed and had no way to stir soldiers' hearts; he then summoned all generals and soldiers at the army gate, ordered his daughter to come out and bow to them, and said, "Generals and soldiers labor in defense; Pi's house has not a foot of goods to give you—only this daughter, fortunately not yet married—I wish to sell her for one day's expense for the generals and soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Pi knew affairs would not succeed and had no way to stir soldiers' hearts; he then summoned all generals and soldiers at the army gate, ordered his daughter to come out and bow to them, and said, "Generals and soldiers labor in defense; Pi's house has not a foot of goods to give you—only this daughter, fortunately not yet married—I wish to sell her for one day's expense for the generals and soldiers."

sentences.zh: 眾皆大哭，曰：「誓為將軍死戰，幸無慮也！」

translations.literal: The multitude all wept loudly and said, "We swear to die fighting for the general—have no worry!"
translations.idiomatic: The multitude all wept loudly and said, "We swear to die fighting for the general—have no worry!"

sentences.zh: 會馬燧與太原之師至，與眾合擊悅於城下，大敗之。

translations.literal: Just then Ma Sui and the Taiyuan army arrived and with the multitude jointly struck Yue below the city, inflicting great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Ma Sui and the Taiyuan army arrived and with the multitude jointly struck Yue below the city, inflicting great defeat.

sentences.zh: 伾乘勢出戰，士卒無不一當百。
